Required a new native lowering in the fastpy compiler: `os.getpid()` → runtime `fastpy_os_getpid` (registered in `codegen.py`; emit handler, `VKind.INT` inference, and `_CSA_MODULE_FUNC_RETURNS` entry) → `objects.c` `fastpy_os_getpid()` → posix `getpid()` → `SYS_PROCESS_ID`. The tool reads `os.getpid()`, writes the decimal PID to `/tmp/fastpy-getpid.out` (via native `open('w')`/`write` → `SYS_FS_*`), and exits 0 iff the PID is `>0`. False-pass-proof **two independent ways**: (1) exit 3 if `getpid()<=0` catches a dead/zero-stub identity; (2) `self_test_fastpy_slateos_getpid` (proc/spawn.rs) reads the written file back and asserts the PID **equals the real PID the kernel assigned at spawn** (`result.pid`) — a stub returning a constant (0, 1, …) would not match the freshly-allocated PID. **Design note discovered during bring-up:** fastpy's `print` lowers to a *direct console-write* syscall that bypasses the linux fd table, so a spawn-time fd-1 redirect cannot capture it (the first attempt printed the PID straight to the console); writing to a real file via `SYS_FS_*` is what lands the value where the kernel can read it back. IR bridge-free (only the `import os`/`import sys` `fpy_cpython_import_native` sentinels; native `fastpy_os_getpid` call present), boot-confirmed (kernel-assigned PID 164 matched exactly). **fastpy `getppid` tool DONE — on-target CONFIRMED (2026-07-22):** `services/fastpy-getppid` (`getppid`), a sibling of `getpid`, exercises the **process-parentage** syscall `SYS_PROCESS_PARENT_ID` — a distinct kernel path from self-identity (`getpid` asks about the caller; this asks about its parent). New native lowering in the fastpy compiler: `os.getppid()` → runtime `fastpy_os_getppid` (registered in `codegen.py`; emit handler, `VKind.INT` inference, `_CSA_MODULE_FUNC_RETURNS` entry) → `objects.c` `fastpy_os_getppid()` → posix `getppid()` → `SYS_PROCESS_PARENT_ID`. The tool writes the decimal parent PID to `/tmp/fastpy-getppid.out` (native `open('w')`/`write`) and exits 0 iff `>0`. False-pass-proof: `self_test_fastpy_slateos_getppid` (proc/spawn.rs) spawns it with `parent=0`; the handler returns 0 for a process with no recorded parent and posix applies the POSIX reparent-to-init convention (0→1), so a correct round-trip yields **exactly 1** — and the harness asserts `== 1`. This cleanly distinguishes the parent syscall from the self syscall: had the lowering mistakenly called `getpid`, the tool would have written its own large PID (165), not 1. IR bridge-free (only the `import os`/`import sys` sentinels; native `fastpy_os_getppid` call present), boot-confirmed (own PID 165, parent PID 1). Then `os.gettid()` → posix `gettid()` → `SYS_TASK_ID` (scheduler task table, a distinct kernel path from the process table): fastpy `services/fastpy-gettid` (5 codegen lowering sites + native `fastpy_os_gettid` in objects.c/runtime.c), false-pass-proof self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_gettid` asserting the tool-written task ID equals the kernel-assigned `result.task_id` exactly (a different ID space than the PID), boot-confirmed (own PID 166, task ID 128 matched exactly). Then the first fastpy **IPC primitive** and first **raw integer-fd** I/O: `os.pipe()` -> posix `pipe()` -> `SYS_PIPE_CREATE` (allocates a kernel pipe + read/write fds), and raw-fd `os.write`/`os.read`/`os.close` on those fds -> posix dispatch by fd kind -> `SYS_PIPE_WRITE`/`SYS_PIPE_READ`/`SYS_PIPE_CLOSE` (a genuinely distinct kernel path from the file/process syscalls the other tools use): fastpy `services/fastpy-pipe` (5 codegen lowering sites + native `fastpy_os_pipe`/`_write`/`_read`/`_close` in objects.c/runtime.c). False-pass-proof self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_pipe` round-trips the NUL-free ASCII constant "PIPE_OK" through the kernel pipe (write end and read end are separate fds connected only by the kernel buffer, so no userspace echo path can fake it) and asserts the file the tool wrote equals "PIPE_OK" byte-for-byte; boot-confirmed (round-tripped 7 bytes intact). **Uncovered + fixed a latent kernel ABI bug in the process:** the native SYSCALL exit path (`syscall_handler_inner`/`entry.rs`) returned only RAX and silently dropped `SyscallResult::value2`, so every two-value syscall (`SYS_PIPE_CREATE`, `SYS_CHANNEL_CREATE`, ...) lost its second return handle to userspace — posix `pipe2()` read leftover garbage from RDX for the write fd, so `os.write` hit `InvalidHandle` and `os.read` blocked forever. Fixed by adding a `has_value2` discriminant to `SyscallResult` (set only by `ok2`) and having the exit path write `value2` into the frame RDX slot when set — delivering the second value for two-value syscalls while preserving the RDX-untouched guarantee normal syscalls need. **Fd-duplication increment done (2026-07-22):** lowered native `os.dup(fd) -> int` (four codegen sites + C `fastpy_os_dup` -> posix `dup()`), the first fastpy os.* to exercise the kernel fd-duplication path. On SlateOS a `dup()` of a pipe fd shares the *same* underlying kernel handle via a fresh fdtable entry (no new kernel object), so a write through the duplicated write-end lands in the same kernel pipe buffer as the original. New `fastpy-dup` tool + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_dup`: writes "DUP_OK" **only through the dup** and reads it from the *original* read-end — false-pass-proof, since the bytes can only survive if `dup` truly aliased the pipe; boot-confirmed (6 bytes round-tripped intact). **Raw-fd file open+seek increment done (2026-07-22):** lowered native `os.open(path, flags[, mode]) -> int` (posix open() -> SYS_FS_OPEN, a raw file fd — the raw-fd counterpart to the high-level builtin `open()` every prior fastpy tool uses) and `os.lseek(fd, offset, whence) -> int` (posix lseek() -> SYS_FS_SEEK, the first fastpy os.* to touch the file-offset seek path). New `fastpy-lseek` tool + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_lseek`: os.open()s a scratch file raw, writes "ABCDEFGH", `os.lseek(fd, 4, SEEK_SET)`, reads 4 bytes — false-pass-proof, since a no-op/mis-lowered seek would read "ABCD" from offset 0 rather than "EFGH" from offset 4; the harness asserts the round-tripped file holds exactly "EFGH". Boot-confirmed (4 bytes read from offset 4; pipe+dup still green, no regressions). **Fd-truncate increment done (2026-07-22):** lowered native `os.ftruncate(fd, length) -> int` (posix ftruncate() -> SYS_FS_FTRUNCATE, the first fastpy os.* to touch the fd-based file-truncate path — a distinct kernel syscall from the path-based os.truncate()/SYS_FS_TRUNCATE and from lseek/write). New `fastpy-ftruncate` tool + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_ftruncate`: raw-opens a file, writes "ABCDEFGH", `os.ftruncate(fd, 3)`, confirms via SEEK_END the new size is 3, rewinds and reads — false-pass-proof, since a no-op/mis-lowered truncate would leave the file at 8 bytes (SEEK_END 8, read "ABCDEFGH") rather than 3 ("ABC"); the harness asserts the round-tripped file holds exactly "ABC". Boot-confirmed (file shrank to 3 bytes; pipe+dup+lseek still green, no regressions). **Positioned-I/O increment done (2026-07-22):** lowered native `os.pwrite(fd, data, offset) -> int` and `os.pread(fd, n, offset) -> str` (posix pwrite()/pread()), the first fastpy os.* to read/write at an explicit absolute file offset *without* moving the fd offset — distinct from write/read + lseek. New `fastpy-pos` tool + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_pos`: writes "ABCDEFGH", `os.pwrite("XY", 2)`, confirms SEEK_CUR is still 8 (pwrite must not advance the fd offset), then `os.pread(4, 1)` -> "BXYE" — false-pass-proof, since an offset-advancing pwrite fails the SEEK_CUR==8 check and an offset-ignoring op yields the wrong bytes; the harness asserts the round-tripped file holds exactly "BXYE". Boot-confirmed (positioned ops hit offsets 2/1 with fd offset left at 8; pipe+dup+lseek+ftruncate still green, no regressions). **Fd-redirection increment done (2026-07-22):** lowered native `os.dup2(oldfd, newfd) -> int` (posix dup2()), which — unlike dup()'s lowest-free-fd — installs a copy of oldfd at the *caller-chosen* newfd (closing whatever was there first), sharing the same kernel handle. New `fastpy-dup2` tool + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_dup2`: dup2()s a pipe write end onto fd 9, writes "DUP2_OK" **through fd 9**, and reads it from the *original* read end — false-pass-proof, since fd 9 is valid only if dup2 installed the pipe handle there (a mis-lowering makes write(9) fail and read(r) block -> harness timeout, never a false pass); the tool also asserts dup2 returned 9. Boot-confirmed (7 bytes through fd 9; all prior fastpy raw-fd tests still green, no regressions). Then added **fastpy-getmtime** (`services/fastpy-getmtime`, ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_getmtime`, caps READ|WRITE|METADATA): the **first fastpy tool to read a timestamp field of the stat struct back into userspace** — `os.path.getmtime(path)` lowers natively to `fastpy_os_path_getmtime` -> posix `stat()` -> SYS_FS_STAT and pulls the *mtime* field (a distinct metadata field from getsize's `st_size`), and it is fastpy's **first `os.*`/`os.path.*` call that returns a float** (CPython-faithful epoch seconds as a `double`) plus the first native `int(<float>)` truncation lowering (`fptosi`). Round-trip self-check in one binary: create the file, `os.utime(path, ns, ns)` stamps a kernel-chosen whole-second mtime (argv-supplied so nothing is baked into the ELF), `got = int(os.path.getmtime(path))` reads it back, and `str(got)` is written to `/tmp/fastpy-getmtime.out`. False-pass-proof three ways: the expected seconds arrive in argv[2] (a stub returning 0.0/const/wall-clock/`st_size` would mismatch and exit 3), whole-second stamps make the float exact (no rounding), and the kernel asserts BOTH exit 0 AND that the written file equals the stamped decimal seconds AND that VFS `modified_ns` matches. Codegen: 5-site native lowering (registration -> DoubleType return; both type-inference paths -> FLOAT; `_os_path_fns` emit map; `_CSA_MODULE_FUNC_RETURNS` -> "float") + `fastpy_os_path_getmtime` C impl in objects.c/runtime.c. Verified bridge-free (only `fpy_cpython_import_native` sentinels). NOTE: the tool must **inline** `int(os.path.getmtime(path))` — binding the float to an intermediate var first drops its FLOAT kind and bridges `int(<var>)` to CPython (tracked as BUG-SCALARKIND-LOST-ON-NATIVE-MODULE-CALL-ASSIGN in fastpy/known-issues.md). Also needed the METADATA right: `sys_fs_stat` requires `Rights::METADATA`, so READ|WRITE alone made getmtime return -1 (stat error) — fixed by granting METADATA (mirrors fastpy-size). Boot GREEN, all prior fastpy tests still green, no regressions). Then fixed the codegen bug the getmtime workaround had exposed (**BUG-SCALARKIND-LOST-ON-NATIVE-MODULE-CALL-ASSIGN**): a *chained* `os.path.*` scalar call assigned to a variable (`b = os.path.getmtime(p)`) was tagged PYOBJ instead of its true scalar kind, so a later `int(b)`/`float(b)`/arith bridged to CPython. Root cause: `_infer_call_type_tag` only recognized native-module method calls when `node.func.value` was a bare Name (`os.getsize(f)`); the three-level form `os.path.getsize(f)` has an Attribute receiver and fell through to the pyobj-receiver fallback. Fix: a chained-form handler mapping the natively-lowered os.path funcs to their kinds (join/basename/dirname→STR, getsize→INT, getmtime→FLOAT, exists/isfile/isdir→BOOL); verified bridge-free via llvm-nm and moved the bug to the Recently-Fixed section of known-issues.md. fastpy-getmtime was then switched to the intermediate-var form (`back = os.path.getmtime(path); got = int(back)`) so it doubles as an on-target regression test. Then added **fastpy-getatime** (`services/fastpy-getatime`, ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_getatime`, caps READ|WRITE|METADATA): the sibling of getmtime that reads the **atime** field of the stat struct (`os.path.getatime` → `fastpy_os_path_getatime` → posix `stat()` → SYS_FS_STAT, pulling `st_atim` — a *distinct* timestamp field from getmtime's mtime). Since `os.utime(path, atime_ns, mtime_ns)` stamps both access and modification times, getmtime validated the mtime half and getatime validates the **atime half** — confirming utime's first (atime) arg is honored and the atime field is independently readable. Same false-pass-proof round-trip (kernel-chosen whole-second stamp via argv, int() truncation, `/tmp/fastpy-getatime.out` written back) with Guard #3 asserting the VFS `accessed_ns` (not `modified_ns`) matches the stamp. Uses the intermediate-var form as another on-target regression test for the scalarkind fix. 6-site codegen lowering + `fastpy_os_path_getatime` C impl; bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions). Then added **fastpy-getctime** (`services/fastpy-getctime`, ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_getctime`, caps READ|WRITE|METADATA) to **complete the get{a,m,c}time trio**: it reads the **ctime** field (`os.path.getctime` → `fastpy_os_path_getctime` → posix `stat()` → SYS_FS_STAT, pulling `st_ctim` from the VFS `changed_ns`). ctime is *distinct in kind* from atime/mtime — it is **not settable via os.utime** (utime stamps only atime and mtime), so this exercises a different validation pattern: the tool stamps atime/mtime to a year-2023 value via `os.utime` and then asserts getctime returned something `!= secs` (proving it read ctime, the real ~2026 creation realtime, not the stamped mtime) and `> 0` (a real value, not the -1.0 stat error or a 0 stub). The kernel self-test additionally reads the VFS `changed_ns` *independently*, asserts it is non-zero and `!= SECS`, and checks the decimal seconds the tool wrote equal `changed_ns / 1e9` — an independent read-back of the exact ctime field (a value the tool could not fabricate). Also uses the intermediate-var form as an on-target regression test for the scalarkind fix. 6-site codegen lowering + `fastpy_os_path_getctime` C impl; bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions). Then added **fastpy-access** (`services/fastpy-access`, ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_access`, caps READ|WRITE|METADATA): the first fastpy tool to exercise **`os.access(path, mode)`** — a genuinely distinct entry point from the stat-field reads. It lowers to `fastpy_os_access` → posix libc `access()` → SYS_FS_STAT and returns a Python **bool** (the first *top-level* `os.*` bool return; the existing bool returns are all `os.path.*`). Crucially the **mode argument is honored**: POSIX `access()` rejects mode bits outside `R_OK|W_OK|X_OK` (`mode & ~7 != 0`) with EINVAL, so `os.access(path, 8)` returns *False even for an existing file* — proving the mode reached the syscall rather than being ignored (a getsize-style existence-only wiring would return True here). The tool probes four cases (F_OK on an existing file → True; R|W|X valid → True; invalid mode 8 → False; F_OK on a missing path → False), writes the 4-char pattern `"1100"`, and exits 0 iff so; the kernel independently confirms via the VFS that TARGET exists and MISSING does not and asserts the exact pattern. 5-site codegen lowering + `fastpy_os_access` C impl (`_fv_from_bool` wrap, i64 mode coercion mirroring chmod); bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions). Then added **fastpy-samefile** (`services/fastpy-samefile`, ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_samefile`, caps READ|WRITE|METADATA): the first fastpy lowering to exercise the **`st_ino`** field. **`os.path.samefile(a, b)`** lowers to `fastpy_os_path_samefile` → two posix `stat()` calls → SYS_FS_STAT and compares the `(st_dev, st_ino)` identity, returning a **bool**. Both stats **follow symlinks** (SlateOS SYS_FS_STAT follows the final link), so a file and a symlink to it are the same file (same inode) while two independently-created files have distinct synthetic inodes. The tool creates TARGET + OTHER and a symlink LINK→TARGET, probes three cases (samefile(TARGET,LINK)→True, samefile(TARGET,OTHER)→False, samefile(TARGET,TARGET)→True), writes the pattern `"101"`, and exits 0 iff so. False-pass-proof: the symlink case is True only if stat() follows the link and inodes are compared (a no-follow or path-string comparison gives False); the kernel independently reads the VFS inode numbers (`FileMeta::ino`, also symlink-following) and asserts `ino(LINK)==ino(TARGET)` and `ino(OTHER)!=ino(TARGET)`, plus the exact "101" pattern. 5-site codegen lowering + `fastpy_os_path_samefile` C impl (2-arg os.path bool wrap); bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions). Then added **fastpy-islink** (`services/fastpy-islink`, ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_islink`, caps READ|WRITE|CREATE|METADATA): the first fastpy lowering to use **`lstat` (no-follow)** semantics. **`os.path.islink(path)`** lowers to `fastpy_os_path_islink` → one posix `lstat()` → SYS_FS_LSTAT (gated on Rights::METADATA) and tests `S_ISLNK(st_mode)`, returning a **bool**. Because `lstat` does not follow the final link, a symlink reports True *even when its target is missing* (the link entry itself exists) — unlike the follow-symlink `exists`/`isfile`/`isdir`. The tool creates a regular file TARGET, a symlink LINK→TARGET, and a *dangling* symlink DANGLING→MISSING (never created), probes four cases (islink(LINK)→True, islink(TARGET)→False, islink(DANGLING)→True, islink(MISSING)→False), writes the pattern `"1010"`, and exits 0 iff so. False-pass-proof: the dangling-symlink True is the decisive discriminator — a follow-symlink `stat()` on a broken link errors and would report False, so only genuine no-follow `lstat` yields True; the kernel independently `Vfs::lstat`s each path and asserts LINK/DANGLING are `Symlink`, TARGET is not, and MISSING does not resolve, plus the exact "1010" pattern. 5-site codegen lowering + `fastpy_os_path_islink` C impl (lstat + S_ISLNK, bool wrap); bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions). Then added **fastpy-stat** (`services/fastpy-stat`, ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_stat`, caps READ|WRITE|METADATA): the **capstone** of the stat-field lowerings. Where getsize/get{a,m,c}time/samefile/islink each read a single field, one **`os.stat(path)`** call → `fastpy_os_stat` → posix `stat()` → SYS_FS_STAT fills the whole struct and returns CPython's `os.stat_result` *sequence* form as a 10-int list `(st_mode, st_ino, st_dev, st_nlink, st_uid, st_gid, st_size, st_atime, st_mtime, st_ctime)` — indexed `st[i]` like os.listdir (raw FpyList* pointer, inference LIST[INT]). The tool writes an 11-byte file, os.stats it, and checks four fields — st[6]==11 (size), st[0]&0o170000==0o100000 (S_IFREG type bits), st[3]>=1 (nlink), st[1]!=0 (ino) — writes the pattern `"1111"`, and exits 0 iff so. False-pass-proof: a constant list cannot simultaneously match the exact size of a just-created file, the S_IFREG type bits, a nonzero inode and nlink>=1; the kernel independently `Vfs::metadata`s TARGET and asserts size==11, ino!=0, entry_type==File. 5-site codegen lowering (registration/inference/emit/CSA, list return like listdir) + `fastpy_os_stat` C impl (fpy_list of 10 fpy_int); bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions). (Note: posix `realpath` does not resolve symlinks — logged in known-issues.md — so no realpath symlink-resolution probe is included.) Then **os.statvfs** (fastpy-statvfs, os commit pending) added a genuinely distinct lowering: filesystem-wide capacity/limits rather than per-file metadata. One os.statvfs(path) → fastpy_os_statvfs → posix statvfs() → SYS_FS_STATVFS returns CPython's os.statvfs_result sequence form as a 10-int list (f_bsize, f_frsize, f_blocks, f_bfree, f_bavail, f_files, f_ffree, f_favail, f_flag, f_namemax), indexed st[i] like os.stat. The fastpy-statvfs tool creates a 1-byte probe on /tmp (memfs), statvfs-es it, checks three invariants (f_bsize>=1, f_frsize==f_bsize, f_namemax>=1) and writes the observed "<f_bsize>,<f_namemax>" decimal pair; the kernel self-test independently Vfs::statvfs-es TARGET and cross-checks BOTH fields exactly against the live filesystem (memfs block_size=1, max_name_len=255, so a constant/guessed stub cannot match both). 5-site codegen lowering (registration/inference/emit/CSA, list return like os.stat) + `fastpy_os_statvfs` C impl (statvfs() → fpy_list of 10 fpy_int, with <sys/statvfs.h>); bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions. Then **os.getuid / os.getgid** (fastpy-getuid) added a genuinely distinct lowering — process **identity**, not filesystem metadata — and made the previously-stubbed posix credential calls real. This required a new **native kernel syscall SYS_PROCESS_GET_CREDENTIALS (529)** (handler packs gid<<32|uid from pcb::get_credentials; registered in dispatch); posix getuid/getgid/geteuid/getegid (unistd.rs) now issue it instead of returning a hardcoded 0; and fastpy os.getuid/os.getgid lower bridge-free to fastpy_os_get{u,g}id → posix → that syscall (5-site codegen + C runtime + externs). The fastpy-getuid tool reads uid/gid and writes "<uid>,<gid>"; the kernel self-test spawns it with a distinct non-root identity (SpawnOptions.uid_gid = (4242, 8181)) and cross-checks the tool's readout against BOTH the spawn-time value and the kernel's stored ProcessCredentials exactly (false-pass-proof: the old 0,0 stub fails, and the two distinct ids rule out a getuid/getgid code-folding coincidence). Required a sysroot rebuild (posix → libc.a) before relinking the ELF. bridge-free; boot GREEN (uid=4242 gid=8181 matched), no regressions. **Increment done (2026-07-22):** native `os.setuid`/`os.setgid` now really *mutate* process identity (previously the posix setuid family were permission-checking stubs that returned success **without changing any credential state**). Added kernel syscall `SYS_PROCESS_SET_CREDENTIALS` (530) — a thin mutation primitive that writes the *calling* process's `ProcessCredentials` (arg0=uid, arg1=gid; sentinel `0xFFFF_FFFF` = leave unchanged); the kernel enforces only “mutate your own process” and policy stays in userspace (POSIX caps are userspace-only, unenforceable by the kernel — see design-decisions §83). posix `setuid`/`seteuid`/`setgid`/`setegid`/`setre*`/`setres*` now run the CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID + identity check then call `unistd::set_real_credentials` → the syscall. fastpy `os.setuid`/`os.setgid` lower bridge-free to `fastpy_os_set{u,g}id` → posix → that syscall (5-site codegen + C runtime + externs). The `fastpy-setuid` tool reads its spawn identity, calls `setuid(3131)`/`setgid(4242)`, reads it back and writes “<u0>,<g0>,<u1>,<g1>”; the kernel self-test spawns it as root (0,0) and cross-checks the readout against BOTH the spawn identity (0,0) and the mutated pair (3131,4242) AND the kernel's stored `ProcessCredentials` exactly (false-pass-proof: the old no-mutation stub leaves creds at 0,0 → two independent failures; distinct non-zero ids rule out a field swap). **Also fixed a latent mm bug this surfaced** (known-issues BUG-CGROUP-1GIB): the per-frame cgroup-id array (`kernel/src/mm/frame.rs`) was a fixed `[u8;65536]` covering only the first 1 GiB of RAM, so frames above 1 GiB were charged but never uncharged (cgroup accounting leak on any >1 GiB machine) — it is now dynamically sized to `total_frames` in the allocator metadata region. Boot-test RAM raised 512M→3072M (the ~47 embedded fastpy self-test ELFs make the kernel image ~202 MiB; 512M no longer fit under Limine). bridge-free; boot GREEN (setuid 0,0→3131,4242 matched; cgroup round-trip OK), no regressions. **Increment done (2026-07-22) — os.nice/os.getpriority/os.setpriority made a REAL scheduler mutation:** previously posix nice/getpriority/setpriority stored the value in a userspace static with ZERO scheduling effect (and the Linux-ABI path wrote an inert pcb.linux_nice field). Added a thin kernel mutation primitive SYS_PROCESS_GET_NICE(531)/SYS_PROCESS_SET_NICE(532) and one authoritative entry point proc::thread::set_process_nice, which writes the PCB nice AND re-prioritises every owning task via sched::set_priority(nice_to_priority(nice)) (map: priority=round((nice+20)·31/39); nice -20→0, 0→16, 19→31). The syscall ABI carries nice biased +20 so it never collides with negative error sentinels. BOTH the native path and the Linux sys_setpriority/sched_setattr fair-nice branch now funnel through set_process_nice, so nice is one real scheduling attribute regardless of ABI. CAP_SYS_NICE policy stays in userspace (posix resource.rs), mirroring the setuid design (§83). fastpy lowers os.nice/getpriority/setpriority bridge-free (fastpy_os_{nice,getpriority,setpriority} → posix nice/getpriority/setpriority). False-pass-proof self-test (services/fastpy-nice, self_test_fastpy_slateos_nice): tool runs as root, setpriority(-7)+nice(-5)→nice -12, writes "0,-7,-12,-12", then SLEEPS (not busy-spin — it raised its own priority above the harness; a spin livelocked the boot); kernel reads pcb::get_nice==-12 AND scheduler base priority==6=nice_to_priority(-12) while the task is alive, then kills it. Old stub would leave get_nice=0 and priority=16 (two independent failures). Design decision §84. Also fixed a boot-test.sh false-pass (BUG-BOOTTEST-BOOTOK-SUBSTRING): unanchored grep matched "BOOT_OK" inside the livelock diagnostic "no BOOT_OK" — now anchored to line start. bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions. **Increment done (2026-07-22) — os.umask made REAL + closed the file-creation-mode ABI gap:** the real blocker was that the native VFS create path IGNORED the caller’s mode entirely — `SYS_FS_OPEN` (610)/`SYS_FS_MKDIR` (604) took no mode arg, so every new file was stamped a fixed 0o644 (dir 0o755) regardless of mode or umask, meaning userspace masking alone would have zero effect. Closed the gap with NEW backward-compatible syscall numbers `SYS_FS_OPEN_MODE` (659, arg3=mode)/`SYS_FS_MKDIR_MODE` (660, arg2=mode) — NOT an arg-overload of the old numbers (syscall3/syscall2 don’t set the extra register, so the ~48 already-built embedded ELFs would pass garbage as the mode and corrupt create perms at boot); old numbers keep default-mode behavior for stale binaries, mode 0 ⇒ historical default. Kernel: `handle::open_with_mode`/`Vfs::mkdir_mode` stamp the caller’s perms verbatim; new `sys_fs_open_mode`/`sys_fs_mkdir_mode` handlers. umask masking stays in the USERSPACE posix wrappers (`apply_umask`: `mode & ~UMASK_VALUE`, default 0o022) which pass the FINAL on-disk bits to the kernel (thin-primitive theme, §83/§84). fastpy `os.umask` lowered bridge-free (`fastpy_os_umask` → posix `umask`). `self_test_fastpy_slateos_umask`: umask(0o077)→prior 18, umask(0o022)→prior 63, then `os.open(mode 0o777)` under mask 0o022 ⇒ **0o755 on disk** (`Vfs::metadata`), distinct from both the 0o644 default and 0o777 request (false-pass-proof both ways). Design decision §85. bridge-free; boot GREEN, no regressions. **/bin promotion of fastpy coreutils DONE — on-target CONFIRMED (2026-07-23):** the demo-track fastpy coreutils were promoted from `/tests` self-test fixtures to real installed `/bin` commands resolved **by command name** through a PATH (`COMMAND_PATH = ["/mnt/bin"]`, where the rootfs `/bin` mounts). New kernel helper `resolve_command(name, PATH)` (spawn.rs) performs the resolve+load step a shell/init does before `exec`; `create-ext4-rootfs.sh` gained a curated `PROMOTED` map that installs each mapped ELF at `/bin/<cmd>` instead of staging it under `/tests` (no ~3.5 MiB duplication). 14 commands promoted across three boot-green batches: read-only `cat wc head tail grep sort uniq ls`, then the FS-mutating set `rm mv mkdir rmdir chmod chown`; each self-test now spawns `argv[0]="<cmd>"` and exercises the real installed-command execution path. The remaining `fastpy-*` self-tests are OS-API probes (getpid/stat/pipe/lseek/umask/statvfs/pkg/…), not user-facing commands, so they stay under `/tests`. Additive & reversible — no Rust coreutil touched. Replace-vs-coexist policy deferred to operator as open-questions Q35 (recommendation: keep additive; never swap a Rust coreutil silently). design-decisions §87. **Exec-primitive increment done (2026-07-23) — userspace-initiated `os.execv`:** `fastpy-run` is the first fastpy program that resolves a command by name over a PATH (`["/nonexistent/bin", "/mnt/bin"]`) via `os.path.exists`, then **replaces its own process image** with the resolved command via `os.execv(path, [cmd, arg])` — the exec primitive a shell/init uses to run a program. The chain lowers bridge-free: fastpy `os.execv` → runtime `fastpy_os_execv` → posix `execv()` → `load_elf()` → `SYS_PROCESS_EXEC` (`exec_process`, reuses the caller's PID so the resolved command inherits the runner's cap table + open handles). Ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_run` stages `/tmp/run-input.txt`, spawns `fastpy-run cat /tmp/run-input.txt`, and asserts the handed-off `cat` echoes the file to serial and exits with its 23-byte count — proving resolve+exec handoff end-to-end. **Fixed a latent kernel DoS in the process:** `parse_packed_strings` pre-allocated `Vec::with_capacity(usize::MAX)` for exec argv/envp (the exec handler passes `usize::MAX` as the "no limit" bound), overflowing the layout computation → `capacity overflow` kernel panic on *any* exec with a non-empty argv; clamped the pre-allocation to `data.len()+1` (known-issues BUG-EXEC-ARGV-CAPACITY-OVERFLOW). **Fork/exec/wait-trinity increment done (2026-07-23) — fastpy `os.fork`/`os.waitpid`:** building on `os.execv`, fastpy gained `os.fork()` (→ posix `fork()` → `SYS_PROCESS_FORK`, COW clone; child returns 0, parent gets the child PID), `os.waitpid(pid, options)` (returns a 2-element list `[pid, status]` that pure mode unpacks like CPython's tuple), and `os.WIFEXITED`/`os.WEXITSTATUS` to decode the status. This completes the classic shell/`init` spawn pattern (fork, `os.execv` in the child, `os.waitpid` in the parent). New `fastpy-forkexec` utility + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_forkexec`: forks a child that `os.execv`s `/bin/cat` over PATH, the parent `os.waitpid`s and propagates the child's exit; the harness asserts the fastpy process exits with `cat`'s 25-byte count — fork/exec/wait proven end-to-end through fastpy's own bindings (distinct from the pre-existing C/Linux-ABI `self_test_linux_fork_execve_wait`). Boots green (BOOT_OK). **Capture/pipeline increment done (2026-07-23):** fastpy `capture` primitive proven — the child `os.dup2(w, 1)`s stdout onto a pipe write end (`os.pipe`), `os.execv`s `cat`, and the parent `os.read`-drains the pipe to EOF, `os.waitpid`s, and cross-checks the captured byte count against cat's exit. This is the last core shell primitive: command substitution `$(...)` and one pipeline stage `cmd1 | cmd2`. Fix: native-ABI `execve` was silently dropping the child's userspace fd->handle table (which holds the dup2 redirect) across `exec`, so redirection was lost — added `SYS_PROCESS_SET_EXEC_FDS`(=1061) so posix `execve` snapshots its live fd table (via `build_fd_map`) and the child's crt0 `SYS_PROCESS_GET_INITIAL_FDS` restores it from a new one-shot PCB field `exec_inherited_fds` (aliases of `ipc_handles`, never closed by the kernel). New `fastpy-capture` utility + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_capture`: captures a staged 23-byte file's output through the pipe and asserts the count. Boots green (BOOT_OK). **Pipeline increment done (2026-07-23):** a genuine two-stage `cmd1 | cmd2` pipeline proven end to end — `fastpy-pipeline` `os.pipe()`s one kernel pipe, `os.fork()`s twice, points the producer's stdout (`dup2(w, 1)`) at the write end and the consumer's stdin (`dup2(r, 0)`) at the read end, then `os.execv()`s each stage (`cat target` upstream, the new `fastpy-countin` stdin-byte-counter downstream), closes both ends, `os.waitpid()`s both children, and cross-checks the producer's byte count against the consumer's. This exercises the *consumer*-side redirect (`dup2(pipe_r, 0)` surviving `execv`) — the direction the `capture` increment never covered (capture only drained the pipe in the parent). Relies on the same `SYS_PROCESS_SET_EXEC_FDS` fd-table-preservation fix. New `fastpy-pipeline` + `fastpy-countin` utilities + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_pipeline`: carries a staged 29-byte file from cat's stdout through the pipe into countin's stdin and asserts the count. Boots green (BOOT_OK). **Redirect increment done (2026-07-23):** the `cmd > file` output-redirection primitive proven — `fastpy-redirect` forks a child that `os.open`s the output file (O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC), `dup2`s it onto fd 1, and `os.execv`s `cat <input>`; the parent reaps, re-opens the output file, and cross-checks the bytes written against cat's exit. Unlike `capture`/`pipeline` (which redirected onto a PIPE handle), this redirects onto a **FILE** handle — a distinct exercise of the `SYS_PROCESS_SET_EXEC_FDS` fix, which must serialise/restore FILE fds across `execve`, not just PIPE fds. New `fastpy-redirect` utility + ring-3 self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_redirect`: `cat` writes a staged 26-byte file's contents into the redirected output file and the harness asserts the read-back count. Boots green (BOOT_OK). With this the core shell I/O-plumbing primitives are complete: exec (`run`), fork/wait (`forkexec`), command-substitution/producer (`capture`), pipeline (`pipeline`), and file redirect (`redirect`). In-redirect increment (2026-07-23): added `fastpy-inredirect` (`services/fastpy-inredirect/build.py`) proving the shell input-redirection primitive `cmd < file` end to end from ring 3 — the child `os.open`s the input file O_RDONLY, `os.dup2`s it onto fd 0 (stdin), and `os.execv`s the consumer (`fastpy-countin`), which reads stdin to EOF and exits with the byte count; the parent reaps it and reads the file back to cross-check. This exercises a readable FILE handle surviving `execve` and being reinstated as fd 0 — the input counterpart to `redirect` (FILE-on-stdout) and distinct from the pipeline consumer (PIPE-on-stdin). Kernel self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_inredirect` asserts the fastpy process exits with the input file length. This closes the exec-fd matrix: both handle types (PIPE, FILE) restored across exec on both standard streams (stdin, stdout). Boots green (BOOT_OK). Minishell composition increment (2026-07-23): added `fastpy-minishell` (`services/fastpy-minishell/build.py`) — the first *composition* binary, which **parses a command line** (`str.split()` tokeniser) and dispatches the simple-command grammar `cmd [args...] [< in] [> out]` through PATH-resolution + `os.fork` + `os.open`/`os.dup2` redirection + `os.execv`, propagating the child exit status like a shell sets $?. Unlike every prior plumbing binary (each proving one primitive directly), this composes them behind a real parser. Fixed a pure-native codegen constraint found along the way: indexing an `append`-built list yields a flexible value whose method calls (e.g. `.find`) route through the CPython bridge (absent in pure mode) → `fpy_fv_call_method1` link error; resolved by capturing the command word from the concrete-`str` loop variable instead of re-reading `argv[0]`. Kernel self-test `self_test_fastpy_slateos_minishell` drives the shell two ways through its parser — `cat IN > OUT` (output redirect with args, verifying the bytes actually landed in the file) and `countin < IN` (input redirect via an absolute-path command) — asserting the propagated exit status equals the input length. Boots green (BOOT_OK). Pipeline increment (2026-07-23): extended the parser to full pipelines — `cmd [args] [< in] [> out] | cmd2 ... | ...` — splitting on `|` into stages wired by `os.pipe()` (stage i's stdout → stage i+1's stdin, an explicit `<`/`>` overriding the pipe wiring), forking every stage, and reporting the LAST stage's exit status as the pipeline's `$?`; a single shell now exercises the exec-fd preservation fix for PIPE **and** FILE fds on **both** standard streams. A second pure-native codegen constraint surfaced here: iterating an element of an `append`-built **nested** list (list-of-lists) yields a flexible value whose iteration routes through the CPython bridge (absent in pure mode) and spins forever in a pure-CPU loop with no syscalls/output. Resolved by a **single flat forward pass** — a sentinel `|` appended to the token list flushes the final stage through the same code path as each `|` boundary, so no list-of-lists is ever built and every construct (flat `append` list, `cmd` from the concrete loop variable, PATH iteration, `argv` handed to `execv`) matches the proven simple-command version. `self_test_fastpy_slateos_minishell` now also drives `cat IN | countin`, asserting the two-stage pipeline delivers the 32-byte count end to end. Boots green (BOOT_OK). Three-stage follow-up (2026-07-23): added `fastpy-catstdin` (`services/fastpy-catstdin/build.py`), a stdin→stdout passthrough filter (`os.read(0)`→`os.write(1)` to EOF), and a fourth minishell sub-test `cat IN | catstdin | countin`. The point of a third stage is the **middle** stage: `catstdin` reads the upstream pipe on fd 0 AND writes the downstream pipe on fd 1 *simultaneously* — a both-ends-are-different-pipes wiring that a two-stage pipeline never puts on one process — proving both inherited PIPE fds survive fork+exec on a single process at once; countin still counts all 32 bytes forwarded through the middle. Boots green (BOOT_OK). Fan-out follow-up (2026-07-23): added `fastpy-tee` (`services/fastpy-tee/build.py`), a `tee`(1) that reads stdin to EOF and writes every byte to BOTH fd 1 AND a file it `os.open`s from `argv[1]` — the **fan-out** pattern (one input duplicated onto two output fds at once), which no prior utility exercised. A fifth minishell sub-test `cat IN | tee OUT` dispatches a pipe-fed stage that also carries its own argv operand (the filename); the harness reads the tee'd file back off disk and byte-matches it to the piped input. Boots green (BOOT_OK). Append-redirect follow-up (2026-07-23): extended the minishell parser to accept `>>` alongside `>`, completing the `< > >> |` redirect grammar. A per-stage `outmode` flag (set by the operator token) selects the `os.open` flags — 577 (O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) for `>` vs 1089 (O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_APPEND) for `>>` — so append exercises a distinct open-flag path no prior sub-test hit. A sixth minishell sub-test seeds an existing file, runs `cat IN >> APP`, and verifies on disk that the file *grew* to hold both copies (2x the content) rather than being truncated; a `>` in the same spot would have left only one copy. This closes the fastpy shell I/O-composition milestone: simple commands, input/output/append redirects, and N-stage pipelines (incl. middle-stage both-ends-pipe and fan-out) all proven end-to-end through a real command-line parser. Boots green (BOOT_OK). **Pure-mode pathlib.Path increment done (2026-07-24):** the high-level Pythonic Path API now works in a no-CPython SlateOS build — runtime/pathlib_pure.c (fastpy repo) implements Path, write_text, read_text, exists, is_file, is_dir, name, suffix, stem, parent, and joinpath (a Path is a heap C string backed by plain stdio over the posix libc SYS_FS_* VFS syscalls), compiled only in pure builds. Two codegen bugs fixed en route (see fastpy known-issues.md): str(Path) raised “requires the CPython bridge” because a Path is OBJ-tagged but its data is a raw char* (generic fastpy_fv_str routed it to the pure-mode bridge stub) — fixed by specializing str() to fastpy_path_str and keeping the PATH tag on Path-returning method calls; and a Path-buffer offset-32 magic collision. Validated on-target by self_test_fastpy_slateos_pathlib (services/fastpy-pathlib/) — a 10-check bitmask, all pass (exit 1023). Boots green (BOOT_OK). **Path-header + iterdir follow-up done (2026-07-26):** the offset-32 collision was first papered over by zero-padding the Path buffer, which only worked while the padding happened to land on the probed word; a Path is now a real **FpyPurePath** struct — a "PATH" magic at offset 0 (so it can't be mistaken for an FpyClosure either), a zero guard word at offset 32 where the OBJ refcount dispatcher probes for FPY_OBJ_MAGIC, and the NUL-terminated path text at offset 40 — so no filename, whatever its bytes, can impersonate a live object. **Path.iterdir()** is implemented too (the one Path method returning a container of Paths): both runtimes materialize an FpyList of OBJ-tagged Paths, and codegen types it list[Path] mode-agnostically so `for f in p.iterdir()` keeps the loop variable Path-tagged. The self-test grew to a 15-check bitmask plus a completion sentinel (exit 65535), covering a filename whose bytes 32..35 spell FPY_OBJ_MAGIC and iterdir entries being both typed and fully joined; it also needed Rights::CREATE|DELETE, since SYS_FS_MKDIR/UNLINK/RMDIR gate separately from plain write. Boots green (BOOT_OK). **Build-system integration verified end to end for the first time since the E: migration (2026-09-10):** the zero-configuration path had been dead for four days -- every fastpy lookup in this tree ended with "or a sibling of the repo root named `fastpy`", which was true at `E:/visual studio projects/os` and false the moment the OS moved to `E:` while fastpy did not (the global CLAUDE.md records fastpy, `Python Agent`, `orchestrator2` and `backup` as still on `D:`). Every fixture build therefore required `FASTPY_DIR` to be set by hand, which is what cost lane A a boot test on 2026-09-10 (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named compiler`). `scripts/ctest-fixtures.py` and `scripts/create-ext4-rootfs.sh` now try the pre-migration location **last** -- after `$FASTPY_DIR`, `$PYTHONPATH` and a real sibling, so a genuine sibling always wins -- and announce it when they use it, because a lookup that silently picks a checkout the caller did not choose is the failure `_fastpy_before` already demonstrated. `scripts/boot-test.sh:772` has the same dead fallback and is lane A's; handed over in `requests/b-a-the-fastpy-sibling-lookup-has-been-dead-since-the-e-migration.md`. **With that fixed, `python scripts/ctest-fixtures.py build` rebuilt all 73 fixtures -- 61 `fastpy-*` utilities and 12 `ctest-*` C fixtures -- in 33 seconds with no environment set at all.** ~~and every one of the 73 came out BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed artifact (`git status` clean across `services/`).~~

**THAT EVIDENCE WAS VACUOUS, corrected 2026-09-16, and the conclusion it
supported is nonetheless true.** There were no committed artifacts to be
identical to: `services/ctest-*/*.elf` and `services/fastpy-*/*.elf` have been
gitignored since **2026-08-21** (`53571a004`, design-decisions S355 -- built on
demand rather than stored). This paragraph was written **2026-09-10**
(`68003e545`), twenty days later. `git status` is clean across `services/` for
ignored files whatever they contain, so the check could not have failed and
therefore measured nothing. A tool that was not looking, reported as agreement.

**Measured properly instead, 2026-09-16.** Hash every fixture, delete all of
them, rebuild from nothing, hash again, diff:

    md5sum services/*/*.elf | sort -k2 > before.txt
    rm -f services/*/*.elf services/*/*.o
    PYTHONPATH=... python scripts/ctest-fixtures.py build     # 77 built, 70s
    md5sum services/*/*.elf | sort -k2 > after.txt
    diff before.txt after.txt

**All 77 byte-identical, 0 differing.** So the AOT toolchain and the C
cross-compile are deterministic across a full rebuild, which is what the
original sentence claimed and could not show. 77 rather than 73 because four
fixtures have been added since.

**But only WITHIN one worktree, and that qualifier is load-bearing.** The same
fixture built in `os-lane-a` and `os-lane-b` differs -- `ctest-pty.elf` is
`c21cd3a8...` here and `27e61539...` there -- because **the absolute source path
is embedded in the binary**: `grep -ao "os-lane-[abc]"` finds `os-lane-b` inside
our copy. Two consequences worth knowing before anyone reuses this:

* a byte-comparison of fixtures is only meaningful within a single checkout, so
  "the other lane's ELF differs from mine" is expected and is not evidence of a
  stale or wrong build. Checking a symbol is present is the cross-tree question
  that *can* be asked;
* the artifacts carry the builder's filesystem layout.

**The staleness signal is still conservative and mtime-based** -- all 73 were
rebuilt in that run because they were "older than `toolchain/sysroot/lib/libc.a`"
and none of them needed to be, so a stale *timestamp* is not evidence of a stale
*artifact*. That part of the original observation stands, and this measurement
is what finally makes it checkable rather than asserted. That is the first measurement of reproducibility for these binaries and it establishes two things at once: the AOT toolchain is deterministic across a rebuild, and the checked-in ELFs are current rather than merely present. It also identifies the staleness signal as conservative and mtime-based -- all 73 were rebuilt because they were "older than `toolchain/sysroot/lib/libc.a`", and none of them needed to be, so a stale *timestamp* is not evidence of a stale *artifact*. Worth knowing before anyone reads that message as a warning. **What remains in this initiative is now in the fastpy repo rather than here:** the OS side builds, links, boots and reproduces; further increments are pure-mode Python surface (`runtime/`, codegen), which is a different tree.

- [-] `[A]` Later: NTFS read support (**done 2026-08-16**, `fs::ntfs` — see §5.2),
  Btrfs read (**done 2026-08-16**, `fs::btrfs`), F2FS read (**done 2026-08-16**,

  which may be a single disk or **one leg of a mirror** (design-decisions §247),
  resolving file attributes through the pool's own SA registry rather than the

  reassembling **gang blocks** — the split allocations a nearly-full pool

- [-] `[A]`+`[B]`+`[E]` **Deferred filesystem operations** — queue a delete or
  rename that cannot happen yet, and remember it across a reboot. Operator's
  request, 2026-09-07. See `roadmap-detailed.md` → "Deferred filesystem
  operations" for the full inventory, and **read its premise note first**: the
  usual motivation ("the file is locked") does **not** apply here, because this
  is a POSIX system and `unlink`/`rename` on an open file already succeed. What
  is worth deferring is a *busy mount*, a *read-only mount*, an *absent
  removable/network volume*, and a full volume that cannot accept a trash
  rename. Three ends to build and one shared entry format, so it wants an agreed
  design before any lane starts. **Design agreed 2026-09-07** in
  `requests/a-cb-deferred-ops-format-agreed-with-notes.md`. The three ends:
  - [x] `[A]` the persistent per-filesystem queue and the VFS hooks that enqueue
    and replay it (2026-09-07). `fs::deferred_ops` — `enqueue()`, `replay()`,
    `cancel()`, `list()`, `replay_on_mount()` hook in `Vfs::mount_with_options`.
    Security: re-checks ACLs against stored UID/GID/groups at execution time;
    drops entries on inode mismatch or permission revocation. 9 self-tests.
    - [x] **The way in, done on lane-a-wip 2026-10-02, awaiting a boot**
      (design-decisions §1529): `SYS_FS_DEFER`/`_LIST`/`_CANCEL` (1126-1128),
      refused at once when the user could not do it anyway; a read-only or
      full volume's entries kept on the system volume under its UUID and
      replayed on mount and on remount read-write; only entries the kernel
      sealed are honoured, and an entry acts only on its own volume (it
      used to replay forged entries as root:
      `A-DEFERRED-OPS-REPLAYED-FORGED-ENTRIES-AS-ROOT`). Lane D's libc entry
      points are next, then `[B]` below.
  - `[B]` `rm`/`mv` offering the deferral when a failure is deferrable —
    interactively only, with an explicit flag for scripts, and never silently:
    a batch job must not queue a deletion that happens an hour after it exits.
    **Blocked (2026-09-24) on a way in:** no system call reaches
    `fs::deferred_ops`, and reading it found that three of the four reasons
    (read-only, full, absent volume) cannot be queued where the queue lives.
    Both are in `requests/b-ade-deferred-ops-needs-a-syscall-and-a-queue-that-can-live-off-the-volume.md`.
    **Kernel half of the way in done 2026-10-02 (lane A, §1529)**; waits on
    lane D's libc entry points.
  - `[E]` the file manager asking in the same dialog that reports the failure,

### 2.4 Networking stack (userspace)
- [-] `[A]` TCP/IP stack (kernel-resident prototype, will move to userspace)
  - [x] Ethernet frame parsing/building
  - [x] ARP request/reply with cache
  - [x] IPv4 packet parsing/building with checksum
  - [x] UDP datagram send/receive with socket layer (32 sockets, 64 queued datagrams)
  - [x] DHCP client (auto-configure IP/mask/gateway/DNS at boot)
  - [x] TCP client (3-way handshake, data transfer, FIN teardown; 32 max connections)
  - [x] TCP server (bind/listen/accept, passive open 3-way handshake; 8 listeners, 16 backlog)
  - [x] DNS resolver (A record queries via UDP)
  - [x] DNS resolution cache (32-entry fixed-size, TTL-based expiration, case-insensitive matching, flush on DHCP renewal, negative caching for NXDOMAIN with 60s TTL)
  - [x] DNS CNAME chasing (follow CNAME chains within responses + follow-up queries, up to 8 hops, cache under original name)
  - [x] DNS query hardening: unique transaction IDs (AtomicU16 counter, prevents spoofed responses), unique ephemeral source ports (49152-65535, prevents port collisions)
  - [x] TCP keepalive probes (RFC 1122 §4.2.3.6): 75s idle, 10s interval, 9 max probes; set_keepalive/set_keepalive_params API; tick from net::poll every 5s
  - [x] TCP receive window tracking: snd_wnd from peer, dynamic advertised_window() based on rx_buffer; send() respects min(cwnd, snd_wnd)
  - [x] TCP RTT estimation (Jacobson/Karels, RFC 6298): SRTT + 4×RTTVAR → dynamic RTO [200ms, 60s]; Karn's algorithm (skip retransmitted)
  - [x] TCP Nagle algorithm (RFC 896): coalesce small segments when unacked data in flight; TCP_NODELAY via set_nodelay()
  - [x] TCP congestion control (simplified AIMD, RFC 5681): slow start → congestion avoidance; cwnd/ssthresh; multiplicative decrease on loss
  - [x] ICMP destination unreachable (13 codes) and time exceeded (2 codes) error handling with human-readable reasons
  - [x] Gratuitous ARP on interface configure (detects IP conflicts, updates neighbor caches)
  - [x] DHCP extended options: lease time, T1/T2 renewal, domain name, NTP server, NAK handling
  - [x] IPv4/TCP/UDP checksum verification on all incoming packets
  - [x] DNS response source validation (IP + port) against spoofed replies
  - [x] DHCP transaction ID randomization (CSPRNG) against LAN spoofing

  - [x] TCP SACK (RFC 2018): SACK-Permitted in SYN, receive-side tracks 4 out-of-order blocks, SACK blocks in ACKs, merge/trim logic

  - [x] TCP duplicate ACK counting + fast recovery (RFC 5681 §3.2): 3 dup ACKs → ssthresh=flight/2, cwnd=ssthresh+3*MSS; additional dup ACKs inflate cwnd by MSS
  - [x] TCP retransmit buffer (64 KiB per connection): stores sent data for retransmission; fast retransmit on 3 dup ACKs sends from buffer; RTO timeout retransmit with exponential backoff (RFC 6298)

The `net.userspace` cutover switch now genuinely works at runtime: fixed a Limine kernel-file request-ID typo (`kernel/src/limine.rs`) that made the boot cmdline — and kernel-file symbolization — silently always empty, and wired `fs::kernparam::init_defaults()` into boot (was only called lazily from the shell). Proven end-to-end via the real cmdline (`cmdline: net.userspace` in limine.conf): switch reads on → persistent daemon spawns (deferred past kernel POST, alongside the container health monitor, so it doesn't perturb the timing-sensitive timeout/hrtimer self-tests), registers `net.stack`, DNS+TCP+UDP parity all green with the NIC owned for the system lifetime; cmdline removed → switch off, resident stack authoritative; both paths pass all boot self-tests (also fixed a latent lost-wakeup in the futex timeout self-test waker, known-issues B-FUTEX-TOWAKER-LOSTWAKE). NOTE: the ring-3 socket-syscall HTTP capstone is now **done and boot-validated switch-on** — a minimal Linux-ABI ring-3 client (`services/httpget`, raw `socket()`/`connect()`/`write()`/`read()`/`close()` over the daemon-backed fd path) is spawned by `run_persistent_netstack` via `spawn_process_with_abi(_, AbiMode::Linux)` (kernel resolves `example.com` and passes the IP as argv), polled to Zombie under a bounded 15s deadline, and its exit code decoded: it returned **0** ("response began with HTTP/1"), i.e. the `dispatch_linux` socket arms (user-pointer copies, fd install, errno mapping) are now exercised from a real ring-3 process end-to-end, not just by code review (serial log `[httpget] start`→`connected`→`OK: HTTP response`, `ring3 HTTP capstone: OK … (exit 0)`). The old blocker — the moving-location container-exec/ring-3 spawn-dispatch race — was root-caused as two holder-preemption raw-`spin::Mutex` deadlocks (heap 83307bdfc, container fa87bbb5e) and fixed (preempt-disable for the hold), validated by 40/40 switch-off + 15/15 switch-on wedge soaks plus this live capstone. 5.7 (flip the default to the daemon) is gated on closing daemon-socket feature parity first (known-issues D-NETSOCK-SYNC) so the flip doesn't regress default networking below the mature kernel stack. Parity progress: the `O_NONBLOCK` **receive** path is now honoured — `recvfrom`/`read` on a nonblocking daemon socket return `EAGAIN` instead of stalling, via a new `netipc::ring::RECV_NONBLOCK` SQE flag + `ERR_WOULD_BLOCK` sentinel drained by the daemon's `ring_tcp_recv`; boot-validated switch-on (`netstack_client::self_test_nonblock_recv` — a non-blocking recv on an idle connected socket returns WouldBlock/EAGAIN promptly). Honest **poll/epoll read readiness** now also lands: a new non-destructive `netipc::ring::OP_POLL` peek (daemon `ring_tcp_poll` → `POLL_READABLE`/`POLL_WRITABLE` bitmask, no bytes consumed) drives `poll_revents_from_entry`'s `Socket` arm via `net::socket::poll_ready`, replacing the old "always-ready" placeholder so `POLLIN` is set only when there are buffered bytes / EOF; boot-validated switch-on (`netstack_client::self_test_poll_ready` — idle socket polls `readable=false writable=true`, then flips to readable once the HTTP response arrives). **Non-blocking connect** now also lands: `connect` on an `O_NONBLOCK` socket follows the Linux `EINPROGRESS → poll(POLLOUT) → getsockopt(SO_ERROR)` dance instead of blocking — new ring ABI `CONNECT_NONBLOCK` flag + `ERR_IN_PROGRESS` sentinel + `POLL_ERR` bit; the daemon grew an async connect state machine (`TcpConn::connect_start` sends the SYN and returns in `SYN_SENT`; `ingest_seg` completes the handshake on the SYN-ACK or latches `connect_failed` on a RST; `poll_connect` retransmits a lost SYN up to `TCP_SYN_ATTEMPTS`; `ring_tcp_poll` reports `POLL_ERR`/`POLL_WRITABLE`); kernel side `NetstackConn::connect(nonblock)` + `poll_ready`→`(readable,writable,error)`, `net::socket::SockState::Connecting` + `connect`→`ConnectOutcome::{Established,InProgress}` (`EISCONN`/`EALREADY` on repeat) + `take_so_error` (one-shot SO_ERROR, `Failed`→`ECONNREFUSED`); syscalls `sys_connect` (O_NONBLOCK→`EINPROGRESS`) + `sys_getsockopt` (`SOL_SOCKET`/`SO_ERROR`) + poll `Socket` arm sets `POLLERR`; boot-validated switch-on (`netstack_client::self_test_nonblock_connect` — EINPROGRESS then polls to writable). **Non-blocking send** now also lands: `send`/`write` on an `O_NONBLOCK` socket returns `EAGAIN` when the send window is full (a prior segment still unacknowledged) and accepts the bytes otherwise — new ring ABI `SEND_NONBLOCK` flag; the daemon's `ring_tcp_send` drains pending ACKs once and returns `ERR_WOULD_BLOCK` on a full window, `ingest_seg` re-opens the window when the peer's cumulative ACK reaches `snd_nxt`, and `ring_tcp_poll` now reports `POLL_WRITABLE` only when the window has room (honest `POLLOUT`); kernel side `NetstackConn::send(nonblock)` maps `ERR_WOULD_BLOCK`→`WouldBlock`, `net::socket::send(_, nonblock)`, and `dispatch_socket_write` reads the fd's `O_NONBLOCK`; boot-validated switch-on (`netstack_client::self_test_nonblock_send`). **Listen/accept server sockets** landed (commit 5c8945607: `OP_LISTEN`/`OP_ACCEPT` ring opcodes, daemon passive-open backlog + in-process software loopback, kernel `net::socket` server-socket fds, boot-green `self_test_listen_accept`). **IPv6 connect** now also lands, closing the last D-NETSOCK-SYNC parity gap: the daemon grew a full TCP-over-IPv6 path with **no state-machine duplication** — `TcpConn` carries an additive `dst6: Option<[u8;16]>` and its `emit`/`recv_one_seg` dispatch on it (`Some`→`send_tcp6`/`recv_tcp_seg6` via the RFC 8200 pseudo-header checksum, `None`→the byte-identical IPv4 path), so handshake/send/ACK/teardown are shared across families; v6 framing (`send_ipv6`/`send_tcp6`, `recv_tcp_any`'s `ETHERTYPE_IPV6` arm → `RawRx::Seg6`), v6 connection demux (`find_by_tuple6`/`route_seg6`/`find_backlog_by_tuple6`), v6 constructors (`connect6`/`connect_start6`/`accept_syn6`), and an IPv6-aware in-process loopback (self-addressed frames to `me.ip6` — the `fe80::/64`+EUI-64 link-local — diverted by IP, bypassing NDP just as the v4 loopback bypasses ARP). New ring ABI `OP_CONNECT6` (16-byte peer address in the SQE data window, port in `aux`); kernel side `NetstackConn::connect6`/`accept6` (18-byte v6 peer window `[ip6:16][port:2]`). Boot-validated switch-on (`netstack_client::self_test_connect6` — full v6 handshake + bidirectional data over loopback, `IPv6 parity ok`). Fixed along the way a latent blocking-`recv` bug in `ring_tcp_recv`: the loop spun the whole `TCP_DATA_ITERS` deadline even with in-order bytes already buffered (harmless for the fast v4 path that stayed under the control-channel timeout, but it pushed the slower v6 loopback round past `RECV_TIMEOUT_NS` → spurious `TimedOut`); it now breaks as soon as `rx_len > 0`, matching `read(2)` semantics. With listen/accept and IPv6 connect both done, all D-NETSOCK-SYNC *daemon-layer* parity gaps are closed. The **AF_INET6 socket-fd connect layer** is now also wired (commit e99fb694f): `sys_connect` on an `AF_INET6` sockaddr parses the 28-byte `sockaddr_in6` (`sin6_port` BE, `sin6_addr` 16 octets) and routes to `net::socket::connect6` → `NetstackConn::connect6` (`socket_connect_from_user` dispatches on `sa_family`: 2→v4, 10→v6, else `EAFNOSUPPORT`), and `getpeername` on a v6-connected socket returns a `sockaddr_in6` (`socket_write_peer_addr6` fed by `net::socket::peer6`/`SocketInner.peer_ip6`); boot-validated switch-on (stream-socket self-test + `IPv6 parity ok` green). The **one remaining socket-fd gap before the 5.7 flip is the server path** — `sys_bind`/`sys_listen`/`sys_accept4` + `SockState::Listening` — which is now **unblocked — Q23 RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (§71 → Option A**: shared, refcounted session; an accepted connection shares the listener socket's ring/session under a distinct `conn_id`, no daemon-ABI change; standing guideline: do not gold-plate this interim path — server sockets get Option A only; see `open-questions.md`), and is the active socket-fd task. Also landed (unblocked, no Q23 dependency): **`getsockname` for daemon sockets (v4 and v6)** via a new `OP_LOCALADDR` ring op — the daemon writes its interface address + the connection's ephemeral `local_port` to the data window (`[ip:4][port_be:2]` v4 / `[ip6:16][port_be:2]` v6), surfaced through `NetstackConn::local_addr` → `net::socket::local` → `sys_getsockname` (Path-B branch; `sockaddr_in`/`sockaddr_in6`, `ENOTCONN` when unconnected); boot-validated switch-on (`self_test_connect6` step 6, `v6 getsockname: local fe80::…:PORT ok`). Also landed (unblocked, no Q23 dependency): **`shutdown(2)` for daemon sockets (v4 and v6)** via a new `OP_SHUTDOWN` ring op — `aux` carries the Linux `how` (`SHUT_RD`/`WR`/`RDWR`); the daemon's `TcpConn` grew `write_shut`/`read_shut` flags (`SHUT_WR` emits our FIN once, later `close` skips re-sending, subsequent `OP_SEND`→`ERR_BROKEN_PIPE`; `SHUT_RD`→subsequent `OP_RECV` reports EOF; honest poll bits), surfaced through `NetstackConn::shutdown` → `net::socket::shutdown` → `sys_shutdown` (Path-B branch: validates `how` after the fd lookup so a bogus fd still wins EBADF; `KernelError::BrokenPipe`→EPIPE); boot-validated switch-on (`self_test_listen_accept` step 6, `shutdown(SHUT_WR)→EPIPE + shutdown(SHUT_RD)→EOF ok`). Also landed (unblocked, no Q23 dependency): **`setsockopt`/`getsockopt` client-option compat for daemon sockets** — `sys_setsockopt` no longer blanket-EBADFs a daemon-backed socket: it accepts the options a typical TCP client (curl/wget/glibc) sets during setup (`SOL_SOCKET`: `SO_REUSEADDR`/`SO_REUSEPORT`/`SO_KEEPALIVE`/`SO_BROADCAST`/`SO_SNDBUF`/`SO_RCVBUF`/`SO_LINGER`; `IPPROTO_TCP`: `TCP_NODELAY`) as no-op successes (the daemon has no per-socket tunables — fixed buffers, always sends each segment immediately), returning `ENOPROTOOPT` (not EBADF) for unknown options; `sys_getsockopt` gained a matching read side beyond the existing `SO_ERROR` (`SO_TYPE`→`SOCK_STREAM`, `SO_RCVBUF`/`SO_SNDBUF`→65536, `TCP_NODELAY`→1, `SO_KEEPALIVE`/`SO_REUSEADDR`/`SO_REUSEPORT`/`SO_BROADCAST`→0, unknown→`ENOPROTOOPT`). Both Path-B branches gate on `userspace_enabled()`+real Socket fd; kernel-context/non-socket fds keep the EBADF terminal. Not a strict 5.7 regression gate (the resident path also stubs these) but a real compat gap on the path to unmodified Linux network programs (the HTTP capstone); boot-clean switch-on. Because 5.7 (flipping the `net.userspace` default) is itself a user-visible, costly-to-reverse policy *and* depends on that Q23-gated server wiring, the netstack-migration thread is at an operator-decision point. Note: reliable switch-on validation still shares the boot host-load sensitivity with the known virtio-blk / container-restart boot flakes (run boot tests one at a time). Also hardened the SHM data path the daemon rings ride on (known-issues D-SHM-MAP-NOCAP, RESOLVED): `SYS_SHM_MAP`/`SIZE`/`CLOSE` now enforce per-region authorization — a userspace caller must be the region's creator or an explicitly-granted PID, else `PermissionDenied`; kernel context stays the TCB. The service registry records each service's `provider_pid` (`service::provider_pid`), and every kernel→daemon ring handoff (`netstack_client::submit_round_on` + the `spawn.rs` bootstraps) calls `shm::authorize(handle, provider_pid(b"net.stack"))` so the daemon keeps mapping its rings while arbitrary processes can no longer map another's region; boot-validated switch-on (daemon pid 227, all SHM-ring parity checks green, no permission errors). Also landed (unblocked, no Q23 dependency): the **AF_INET/AF_INET6 `SOCK_DGRAM` (UDP) socket-fd path** — `sys_socket` now creates a real daemon-backed datagram socket for `SOCK_DGRAM` with protocol 0/`IPPROTO_UDP` (UDPLITE=136 stays `ENOSYS`, unimplemented — the daemon speaks plain UDP, so it is not silently aliased), via `net::socket::{create_dgram,dgram_bind,dgram_send_to,dgram_recv_from}` over the daemon's `OP_UDP_{BIND,SEND,RECV}` ring ops (in-band 24-byte source-address header on recv); `sys_bind`/`sys_sendto`/`sys_recvfrom`/`sys_getsockname` grew Path-B datagram branches (`bind` auto-binds an ephemeral local port, `sendto` requires a destination sockaddr → `EDESTADDRREQ`, `recvfrom` returns the copied count with the real per-datagram source written to the caller's `sockaddr_in`, poll/epoll readiness via the generic `poll_ready` Dgram arm); the socket-gate self-tests (`socket EPROTONOSUPPORT gating`) were made switch-aware for the DGRAM/UDP case. Proven from a real ring-3 process by a new **`services/udpget` capstone** (bare Linux-ABI ELF: `socket(SOCK_DGRAM)`/`bind`/`sendto`/`recvfrom` a DNS `A?` query, result decoded from exit code), spawned by `run_persistent_netstack` and boot-validated switch-on (`[udpget] start`→`query sent`→`OK: DNS reply`, `ring3 UDP capstone: OK … (exit 0)`). With this, the datagram socket-fd surface reaches parity with the stream path (the only remaining pre-5.7 socket-fd gap is the Q23-gated server path). **AF_INET6 UDP datagrams now also work** (the datagram sibling of the `connect6` work): all five layers landed — netproto `udp::write_v6`/`Datagram::parse_v6` (mandatory v6 checksum, RFC 8200 §8.1); a new `netipc::ring` `OP_UDP_SEND6` opcode carrying the 16-byte v6 destination in-band at the front of the data window (`[dst_ip16:16][payload…]`, port in `aux`) since it doesn't fit in the SQE `aux`; the daemon's UDP queue made family-tagged (`UdpDatagram`/`UdpSock` carry `family`+`src_ip:[u8;16]`, `recv_udp_any` grew an `ETHERTYPE_IPV6` arm that parses/validates against `me.ip6` and tags v6, `udp_sock_send6` emits via `send_ipv6`); the kernel client's `udp_send_to6` + a unified `udp_recv_any` returning `(res, family, ip16, port)`; and `sys_sendto`/`sys_recvfrom` sockaddr_in6 dispatch (28-byte `sockaddr_in6` parse on send, **family-aware recvfrom** that writes `sockaddr_in6` for a v6-sourced datagram and `sockaddr_in` for a v4-sourced one — family is a per-packet property from the daemon RX header, not the socket domain). Recv reuses the existing 24-byte in-band source header (already family+16-byte-IP capable). Boot-validated switch-on via `netstack_client::self_test_udp6_loopback` (bind :9201, send to the EUI-64 link-local `me.ip6`, receive own 28-byte datagram back, assert `AF_INET6` family + matching source + payload) using the daemon's IPv6 in-process loopback divert (self-addressed frame to `me.ip6`, bypassing NDP). **UDP `connect()` default-peer now also works** (v4 and v6): `connect(2)` on a `SOCK_DGRAM` fd records a default peer (no handshake, auto-binds a source port) via `net::socket::dgram_connect` (new `DgramPeer::{V4,V6}` + `SocketInner.dgram_peer`), so `send`/`write`/`sendto(NULL dest)` target it (`dispatch_dgram_send_connected`; `EDESTADDRREQ` when unconnected) and `recv`/`read` filter to it (`dgram_recv_from` drops non-peer datagrams, as Linux does on a connected UDP socket); `sendto` *with* an address still sends there; `getpeername` reports the peer (`ENOTCONN` otherwise); `connect(AF_UNSPEC)` dissolves it. Boot-validated switch-on by `netstack_client::self_test_udp_connect` (connected send loops back + passes the peer filter, `getpeername` matches, a non-peer-port datagram is dropped by the connected receive). **v6 `getsockname` family reporting now also works**: `net::socket` records the creation `domain` on every socket (`SocketInner.domain`, set by `create`/`create_dgram`, read via `socket::domain`), so `sys_getsockname` on an `AF_INET6` datagram socket writes a `sockaddr_in6` (`[::]:port`) instead of always emitting `sockaddr_in` (`0.0.0.0:port`); v4 datagram sockets still report `0.0.0.0:port` and stream sockets are unaffected (they carry the family in the daemon-assigned endpoint). **The AF_INET6 arm of the ring-3 `udpget` capstone now also lands**, closing the last UDP follow-up: `udpget` grew a v6 loopback mode (`socket(AF_INET6,SOCK_DGRAM)`/`bind([::]:port)`/`sendto([me.ip6]:port)`/`recvfrom`, selected by a 4th argv `"6"`; since slirp has no v6 upstream it self-loops through the daemon's IPv6 in-process divert and asserts the exact payload echoes back with an `AF_INET6` source); the kernel derives `me.ip6` from the NIC MAC and passes it as a 32-hex argv, and `run_ring3_udp6_capstone` spawns/decodes it — boot-validated switch-on with **exit 0** (`[udpget] OK: v6 loopback echo`, `ring3 UDP6 capstone: OK … (exit 0)`), so the ring-3 `sockaddr_in6` sendto/recvfrom dispatch path is now exercised live. With this, all documented UDP daemon-socket follow-ups are closed; the only remaining pre-5.7 socket-fd gap is the server path (bind/listen/accept), now unblocked (Q23 resolved → Option A). **The server socket-fd path is now DONE (Q23 Option A):** `net::socket` grew `SockState::Listening`, `bind_stream`/`listen`/`accept`/`is_listening`/`stream_local_port`, and a shared refcounted ring session (`SessionRef::Owned`→`Shared(SharedConn)` behind `Arc<Mutex<NetstackConn>>`) — a listening socket keeps its daemon session under `LISTENER_ID`=100 and each `accept` installs a **new** fd/socket that shares the same ring under its own `conn_id` (`ACCEPT_ID_BASE`=101+), so **no daemon-ABI change** is needed. The Linux syscall layer routes `bind(2)` (stream) → `bind_stream` (`socket_stream_bind_from_user`), `listen(2)` → `net::socket::listen` (`OP_LISTEN` + Owned→Shared conversion), `accept(2)`/`accept4(2)` → `net::socket::accept` (`socket_accept_from_user`: installs the accepted fd, honours `accept4`'s `SOCK_CLOEXEC`/`SOCK_NONBLOCK`, writes the peer `sockaddr_in`/`_in6` when the addr ptr is non-NULL, maps empty backlog → `EAGAIN`; a *blocking* listener retries via `yield_now` since object-layer `accept` is single-shot), and `getsockname(2)` on a listener reports `0.0.0.0`/`[::]`:port via `stream_local_port`. Accepted-connection teardown sends a per-`conn_id` `OP_CLOSE` (`NetstackConn::close_conn` via `SharedConn::Drop`) so accept+close loops don't leak daemon state; the listener's `OP_STOP` still fires on the final `Arc` drop. Boot-validated switch-on: the ring-level data path by `netstack_client::self_test_listen_accept` and the object-layer state machine (bind→listen→accept, port reporting, idempotent re-listen, empty-backlog EAGAIN, dgram/listening op rejection) by the new `net::socket::self_test_server` (`[net::socket] Server-socket (bind/listen/accept) self-test PASSED`). **Interim concurrency limitation (deliberate, Option A, known-issues D-NETSOCK-SYNC):** the listener and all its accepted connections share ONE SPSC daemon session serialized by a single lock, so concurrent I/O across accepted connections is serialized (head-of-line blocking) — acceptable for the interim synchronous-socket path; the future async socket server removes it. **With the server path done, ALL pre-5.7 socket-fd gaps are closed** — 5.7 (flipping the `net.userspace` default) is now gated only on the operator's user-visible policy decision.

Kernel side (kernel/src/proc/signal.rs): per-process SignalState (pending u64, blocked u64, trampoline addr) in a BTreeMap, PENDING_COUNT atomic fast-path, lazy delivery at syscall-return via deliver_pending_signal() which builds a SignalContext on the user stack and redirects RIP to the registered trampoline (mirrors SEH exception delivery). Syscalls SYS_SIGNAL_REGISTER(522)/SEND(523)/RETURN(524, frame-modifying)/MASK(525)/PENDING(526). classify_post() decides Deliver/Terminate/Drop; SIGKILL always fatal; default-action fallback when no trampoline. Userspace side (posix/src/signal.rs): SignalContext mirrors kernel ABI (136B), __signal_trampoline (global_asm) + __signal_dispatch runs dispatch_self_signal then SYS_SIGNAL_RETURN; init_signals() registers trampoline from __libc_start_main; kill() cross-process routes ALL valid signals through SYS_SIGNAL_SEND (sender no longer classifies by disposition — kernel+target decide); sigprocmask mirrors low-64 blocked mask to kernel; sigpending queries kernel. The kernel's real per-process encoder exists but is registered only on the Linux ABI table. Logged as `known-issues.md` → `TD-POSIX-NATIVE-GETRUSAGE-REPORTS-SYSTEM-WIDE-CPU`, filed as `requests/b-a-native-getrusage-reports-system-wide-cpu-as-per-process.md`.   - [x] job-control stop: the `Stop` default action (SIGSTOP/SIGTSTP/SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU) suspends the process for real via `SYS_SIGNAL_STOP_SELF` (1062) and returns only on SIGCONT — 2026-08-12. Deliberately *not* `SYS_SIGNAL_SEND(self, SIGTSTP)`: the kernel's send path tests `has_trampoline` before it reaches the catchable stop signals, and a native process always has one, so a self-send would loop in the dispatcher instead of stopping. The dedicated number also lets the wait status name the signal that actually stopped us (Ctrl-Z must report SIGTSTP, not SIGSTOP). Self-only by construction — no pid argument, so no new route to the `CAP_KILL`-gated cross-process stop. Coverage: `dispatch::test_dispatch_signal_stop_self_rejects_non_stop_signals` (rejection path only; the accept path parks the caller, so it cannot run from the kernel self-test task) plus posix unit tests.
  - [x] job-control wait: `waitpid`'s `WUNTRACED`/`WCONTINUED` are honoured rather than merely accepted, via `SYS_PROCESS_WAIT_STATUS` (1063) — 2026-08-12. A new number rather than extra arguments on `SYS_PROCESS_WAIT` (501): 501 returns the exit code in `rax`, where every value is a legal exit code and there is no encoding left for "stopped", and its existing 1-arg callers leave stale register contents that a new options word or status *out-pointer* would read — and write through. `sys_wait4`'s blocking loop moved down into `handlers::wait_for_child_event` and both wstatus encoders into `pcb`, so the native and Linux ABIs read the same records through the same code and cannot disagree about which child changed or how it is described. **Completed 2026-08-16:** the unification finished — `wait4`, `waitid` and 1063 now share one primitive (`kernel/src/syscall/wait.rs`), with a `WaitTarget {Any,Pid,Pgid}` enum replacing the overloaded selector. That closed lane B's `requests/b-a-waitid-needs-an-explicit-idtype-wait.md`: new `WPGID` (1<<16) makes group 1 nameable, `WNOWAIT` (1<<24) peeks without reaping, a new `WaitInfo` out-parameter (`arg3`/`arg4`, 72 bytes, `clone3`-style min-size convention) carries the child's uid and six usage counters, `wait4` writes a real `rusage` instead of zeroing it, and `waitid` fills `si_utime`/`si_stime` — and, unasked, became *interruptible* (it previously had no signal handling at all). See `design-decisions.md` §206.
  - [x] job-control end-to-end (ring 3): `services/ctest-jobctl` — a child `raise(SIGTSTP)`s itself, its parent's *blocking* `waitpid(WUNTRACED)` is woken with `WIFSTOPPED`/`WSTOPSIG == SIGTSTP`, `kill(child, SIGCONT)` resumes it into a `WIFCONTINUED` report, and the resumed child runs to completion — 2026-08-12. Decodes with musl's own `W*` macros, so the kernel's status encoding is checked against a third party's definition. This is the only layer that can see the feature: the host suite gets `ENOSYS` for every stop (`stop_self`'s syscall arm is target-only) and the kernel dispatch self-test can only ever pass `WNOHANG`, since a real stop on the boot thread would park the one task left to resume it. Run by `spawn::self_test_jobctl`.
