  - [x] Process group tracking: originally PGID/SID/foreground-PGRP in userspace statics with lazy init. **Superseded 2026-08-12**: PGID and SID now come from the kernel process table via native syscalls 533-536 (the statics are deleted — they let a parent and its child disagree about the child's own group; see `known-issues.md`, TD-POSIX-PROCESS-GROUPS-ARE-FAKE-FOR-NATIVE-ABI-PROGRAMS). The foreground PGRP followed on the same day: `FG_PGRP` is deleted too, and `tcgetpgrp`/`tcsetpgrp` plus `ioctl(TIOCSCTTY/TIOCNOTTY)` now go through native syscalls 537-540 to a per-session kernel table (`pcb::CTTY_FG_PGRP`). The old "local rather than wrong" rationale recorded here was itself wrong: the foreground group existed in *three* unrelated places — this static, `tty::FOREGROUND_PGID` (what `^C`/`^\` actually signalled, written only by the Linux shim's `TIOCSPGRP`), and nothing at all for the native ABI — so a shell and the job it foregrounded, and a glibc program and a slateos-libc program, could disagree indefinitely.
  - [x] Controlling terminal (2026-08-12): the foreground process group belongs to a *session*, not a process, so it lives in one kernel table keyed by SID (`pcb::CTTY_FG_PGRP`; locking order — never taken while `PROCESS_TABLE` is held). Native syscalls `SYS_TTY_GET_PGRP`/`SET_PGRP`/`ACQUIRE_CTTY`/`RELEASE_CTTY` (537-540); the Linux shim's `TIOCGPGRP`/`TIOCSPGRP` read/write the same state, and `TIOCSCTTY`/`TIOCNOTTY` are really implemented instead of silently accepted. `setsid()` drops the terminal; the last exit from a session releases it; `TIOCNOTTY` by the session leader hangs up the foreground group (SIGHUP then SIGCONT, Linux `disassociate_ctty` parity). `tty::foreground_pgid()` — the value `^C`/`^\` signal — is now a derived read of that table. **Deferred**: `SIGTTIN`/`SIGTTOU` enforcement on background reads/writes (the predicate `pcb::ctty_is_background` exists; the enforcement points do not — **done later the same day**, see the terminal-access job control entry below); the Linux `TIOCSCTTY` steal flag (no credential model yet); per-process `TIOCNOTTY` (needs a per-process ctty pointer). `Ctrl-Z` is *not* deferred — `tty::feed` already turns `VSUSP` into `SIGTSTP` the same way it turns `VINTR` into `SIGINT`, and `deliver_console_signal` already sends it to the (now correct) foreground group. See `todo.txt`. Tested at all three layers: host unit tests (argument handling), `pcb::test_controlling_terminal` + `dispatch::test_dispatch_ctty_syscalls` (kernel side), and the ring-3 fixture `services/ctest-ctty` — the only layer that can show the state is *shared*: a forked child reads its parent's group before the handoff and its own after `tcsetpgrp(0, child)`, which a per-process static could never report. The fixture exits still holding the console so `self_test_cctty` can assert the release-on-session-exit half from the kernel side.
  - [x] Terminal modes and console reads reach the kernel (2026-08-12): the native ABI could not see the terminal's real state at all — `tcgetattr` returned a constant `default_termios()`, `tcsetattr` wrote a userspace static the kernel never read (so raw mode was a no-op: `getch()`-style input still echoed and still waited for Enter), and `read()` on a console fd used `SYS_CONSOLE_READ_CHAR` (101), which bypasses the line discipline entirely — no canonical mode, no backspace, no `^C`/`^\`/`^Z`. Same bug shape as the foreground-process-group entry above: the real state lived in the kernel, the Linux shim used it, and the native ABI kept a local copy that lied. Fixed by native syscalls `SYS_TTY_GET_TERMIOS`/`SET_TERMIOS`/`READ` (541-543) onto the same `tty::TERMIOS`/`tty::console_read` the Linux shim's `TCGETS`/`TCSETS`/`read` use; the read path is shared as `handlers::tty_read_into_user` (returning `TtyReadOutcome`) and `deliver_console_signal` moved from `linux.rs` into `handlers.rs`, so the two ABIs differ only in error encoding and cannot drift on what counts as a line, an EOF, or a signal character. `SYS_TTY_READ` is the **first native syscall to emit a restart sentinel** (`-ERESTARTSYS` after a signal character) — safe because `entry.rs` applies `resolve_syscall_restart` to both ABIs' results, and `deliver_pending_signal` folds the sentinel to `-EINTR` when a native handler runs. posix marshals between the two wire formats explicitly (`termios_to_wire`/`termios_from_wire`): musl's *user* `struct termios` is 60 bytes (`NCCS`=32 plus `c_ispeed`/`c_ospeed`) while the kernel's `TCGETS` wire format is Linux's 36 (`NCCS`=19, `c_line`, baud folded into `c_cflag`'s `CBAUD` bits) — a memcpy would have corrupted. `default_termios()` survives only as the initial state and the host test-double's seed. See `design-decisions.md` §114. Still absent (at the time): `SIGTTIN`/`SIGTTOU` enforcement — done in the entry below — and a TTY *device* layer (`/dev/tty`, PTYs) — a line discipline is not a tty driver; this closes the ABI gap, not the device gap.
  - [x] Terminal-access job control — `SIGTTIN`/`SIGTTOU` (2026-08-12): the last of the three pieces the controlling-terminal entries above deferred. A background process that reads the terminal is sent `SIGTTIN`; one that writes with `TOSTOP` set, or calls `tcsetattr`/`tcsetpgrp` (unconditionally — `TOSTOP` governs background *output* only), is sent `SIGTTOU`. Modelled on Linux's `__tty_check_change()`, including its two easily-inverted asymmetries: the signal goes to the **caller's own** group, not the terminal's foreground group; and when the signal is ignored or blocked a *read* fails `EIO` while a *write* is let through. The policy is a pure function (`handlers::tty_job_control_decide` → `Allow`/`Signal`/`Fail`) with a thin effectful wrapper (`tty_job_control_check`), because the effectful form asks about the *calling* process and the kernel self-test task owns no process — without the split every branch would have been untestable outside ring 3. The blocked-signal check is a **liveness** requirement, not an errno refinement: a blocked `SIGTTIN` is undeliverable, so raising it and returning `ERESTARTSYS` would restart the read and spin in the kernel forever. Enforcement points: `sys_tty_read`, `sys_console_read_char`, `sys_console_write` (gated on the new `tty::lflag::TOSTOP`), and the new shared `tty_set_termios_from_user`/`tty_set_pgrp_checked`, which the Linux shim's `TCSETS`/`TCSETSW`/`TCSETSF`/`TIOCSPGRP` arms now delegate to instead of keeping their own copies of the bodies. **Known limitation, deliberate**: the kernel can see a process's blocked mask and its no-trampoline default action exactly, but an explicit `SIG_IGN` only for `AbiMode::Linux` — native dispositions live in userspace by design (the reason `SYS_SIGNAL_STOP_SELF` exists). So a job-control shell on our native libc must *block* `SIGTTOU` around `tcsetpgrp` rather than ignore it; see `todo.txt` item 1a. Two latent bugs fell out: `linux_from_native` was flattening the `-512` restart sentinel to `EINVAL` (reachable the moment console *writes* could be gated), and posix's `ctty_errno` mapped `IoError`/`Interrupted` to `ENOTTY` — which tells a shell "not interactive, skip job control", the opposite lesson to draw from being stopped for touching the terminal. Tested by `dispatch::test_dispatch_tty_job_control` (all four cases incl. the orphaned group) and ring-3 checks 72-86 of `services/ctest-ctty`. See `design-decisions.md` §115.
