All four kinds of progressive scan (DC first/refinement, AC first with end-of-band runs, AC refinement) gather every block's coefficients across the passes, then reconstruct through baseline's own dequantise/IDCT/upsample path, so a progressive file decodes to exactly the pixels of its baseline twin — tested bit for bit over six Pillow-written pairs, full size and scaled. A thumbnail keeps only the coefficients its scaled transform reads plus a non-zero mask (10 bytes a block at 1/8 scale instead of 136); a file cut off early shows the passes that arrived. design-decisions.md §1305.
  - [x] `[F]` **JPEG colour comes back the way every other decoder brings it back** — a photograph's colour is usually stored at half resolution, and this decoder repeated each sample where libjpeg (under every browser and image library) blends neighbours with its triangle filter, so colour edges came out stepped, up to 105 levels from any other program's picture of the same file. `gui/imagecodec/src/jpeg/upsample.rs` transcribes libjpeg-turbo's filter exactly — its rounding, its edges, and when it does not filter — held bit for bit against a literal transcription of libjpeg's loops, and every colour layout (4:4:4, 4:2:2, 4:2:0, 4:4:0, 4:1:1, grey, planes too narrow to filter) to within 3 levels of libjpeg-turbo's own decode. About as fast as before (whole picture, release: 4:2:0 1.07 s → 0.97 s, 4:2:2 1.26 s → 1.31 s). design-decisions.md §1306.

It now does what libjpeg-turbo does — each reduced sample the mean of the square it stands for (`jidctred.c`), and 4:2:0 colour reconstructed at the output's resolution rather than upsampled (`jdmaster.c`) — so every fixture at every scale is within 2 levels of TurboJPEG's own scaled decode, which the tests now hold it to. Held exactly — GIF is lossless — over nineteen fixtures, every frame: Pillow-written files answered by Pillow where it agrees with browsers, and hand-written ones (an uncleared full dictionary, mid-string clears, no colour table, frames off the canvas…) answered by the indices they were made from. 1.6 ms a frame for a 480x360 animation, half Pillow's time. design-decisions.md §1308; `requests/f-ce-gif-decodes-and-animates.md`.

It is fitted on every event and frame now, the selection is kept in sight in rows of the view showing, and the rows, the scrollbar and the column header are the listing's part of the pane -- the bar sat over the preview when it was open on the right.
  - [x] `[C]` **Queue a copy/move against a drive another operation is already using, instead of running both at once.** When the user starts a directory copy or move whose source *or* destination is on a drive that an in-flight operation is already reading from or writing to, do not start it -- put it in a queue and run it when the operation ahead of it finishes. Two reasons, and the second is the important one: concurrent operations on one drive are *slower* than the same work done one after another (they interleave two access patterns into one device queue, which on a spinning disk means seeking between them and on any device means neither stream gets a contiguous run), and a machine with fewer operations in flight has fewer that can be left half-done by a crash, a power loss or an accidental abort. Queued operations are visible in the "File Operations" / Transfers view with what they are waiting on, and the user can reorder them, start one anyway, or cancel it. Full description in `roadmap-detailed.md` section 4.1. — **done 2026-09-14.** Four parts, and the first three were prerequisites nobody had noticed. **(a)** `OperationExecutor` ran the whole operation in one call *inside an event handler*, so the explorer froze for the length of any copy, the progress it was already computing could never be drawn, and there was no such thing as an operation in flight to arbitrate between — split into `begin`/`step`/`finish`, with the loop body and the Move source-deletion phase *moved rather than retyped*, since that phase deletes the user's sources and its guard records an earlier version that deleted the wrong ones. **(b)** A step was a whole *file*, so one large file still held the window — a `CopyCursor` and a megabyte chunk fixed that, with the chunk **filled** rather than read once, because `Read::read` may return short at any time so only a short *fill* is the end of a file; the partial bytes stay in the temporary until the last one lands, so a cancelled copy leaves nothing wearing the real name. **(c)** `same_device` existed **twice** and both copies compared the path's first component — which on a Unix-shaped filesystem is `/` for every absolute path, so every drag resolved to "same device" and therefore to **Move**, including a drag off a camera card. The test that covered it asserted the gap rather than closing it (*"on our OS different mount points would have different first components"* — they would not), and it only passed because the host is Windows, where a drive letter *is* the first component. `apps/explorer/src/drives.rs` resolves it once, properly, and `same_drive` answers `Option<bool>` because the two callers want **opposite** conservative readings of not knowing: a drag that cannot tell should Copy (a duplicate is recoverable, a move off a card is not) and a queue that cannot tell should serialise. **(d)** Then the rule itself: `OperationPlan::drives` resolves both ends of every path into a `DriveSet` (one `stat` per directory, not per file), `start_operation` admits an operation that shares no drive and queues one that does, `admit_pending` scans *past* a blocked operation so one on a free drive does not wait behind it, and the frame's eight milliseconds are split between however many run. Escape stops everything — the running operations, which end with every file wholly moved or wholly not and their journals kept for a resume, and the waiting ones, which cost nothing because nothing was written. **A claim withdrawn on the way, which is the part worth keeping:** this was filed as blocked on threading, on the reasoning that `fs::copy` blocks and the explorer has one thread so the drive rule "would be a rule with no effect". That skipped a step — writes go to a page cache, so interleaved copies *can* keep two devices busy, and whether they do here is **unmeasured**. No threads were needed. What is still open is only the throughput question, and the correctness half never depended on it. Not yet done from 4.1's description: reordering the queue and starting a queued operation early, which want a Transfers view rather than a status line. 363 explorer tests; design ties in `known-issues.md`.
  - [x] `[C]` **Six programs stopped inventing what they showed you** — a sweep, not a feature, and every one was found by the same question: *what fills this?* **`apps/settings` on five pages.** Sound listed devices that do not exist. **Updates** said "Your device is up to date" in green, unconditionally, from code that had never looked; its "Check for Updates" button ran `self.checking_for_updates = !self.checking_for_updates` and nothing else; and it listed four installed updates with Windows-style KB numbers, one of them a *failed* GPU driver update and one a "Cumulative update for .NET runtime" on a system with no .NET. **The failed entry is what set the priority:** a fabricated success is a lie about nothing, and a fabricated failure sends someone hunting a problem on their own machine that never happened, with no way to learn it was never real. **Accounts** listed Alice, Bob and Charlie with `@example.com` addresses, login counts of 142/56/23 and one marked a child account under "Screen time limits and content filters are active"; this one was **wired rather than gutted** — `gui/loginusers` already reads the real database for the login screen and lockscreen — with `new()` left pure and `main` calling `load_user_accounts`, matching the existing `load_appearance`/`load_input`/`load_notifications` split, because a constructor that reads a file makes every test depend on the machine it runs on. Email, login count and the child account had no source and went. **Privacy** drew a tick-and-cross table over nine non-existent programs — `Browser` ticked for Camera — and **could not be finished, only removed**: `design.txt` specifies capability security with no ambient authority, so a per-application permission list is not this system's model half-built but Windows' model borrowed, and completing it meant building a store the kernel does not consult. **Network** showed `eth0` connected at 192.168.1.100 with a green link dot on a system that cannot enumerate interfaces; its address and DNS fields would have been dead anyway, since `net/dns` defines a `ResolverConfig` and parses `resolv.conf` and no program loads one. **`apps/photomanager` was the sixth and the sharpest**, because the fabrication was not a panel but the whole application: `main` called `seeded_library()` — two albums, three photos, and `ExifData::sample`, a Canon EOS R5 with GPS coordinates in San Francisco — under a comment saying "so the first window is not an empty grid". It had no file picker at all, so that library was the only content it could ever hold, while `parse_exif_from_bytes` sat written and tested and had never been given a file that existed. Import now opens guitk's `FileDialog` filled by `list_directory` (widget pure, host reads the directory), reads the bytes, parses the EXIF and imports; a failed read says so in the status bar, because an import that changes no count and offers no reason cannot be told from one that never happened. Then the seven EXIF fields the parser decoded and never displayed — focal length, flash, GPS altitude, software, copyright, exposure program, exposure bias — became rows, in that order deliberately: "show them or stop reading them" had no answer until the app could open a real photograph, and displaying them first would have surfaced more of the Canon. **Two findings about tests came out of it.** Emptying the accounts list turned six tests red at once, every one of which had silently been using the three invented accounts as its fixture — and they only surfaced because the list became *empty* rather than merely different; three real accounts would have kept them green against whatever the machine had. And removing the network adapters killed three tests genuinely about adapters plus six that clicked an adapter row only as a *vehicle* for testing the shipped `run` loop, which were re-pointed at an account row rather than deleted with the feature. **Tooling:** `check-fields-written-never-read.py` now also reports a field read by **nobody** — its condition required a test read, so the stricter case fell outside a detector named for it — and `dead_code` cannot see those either, because a `#[derive(Debug)]` reads every field. Baseline 54 → 47. 5,000+ lines deleted across the six. known-issues.md `TD-C-THE-UPDATE-PAGE-INVENTED-ITS-HISTORY-AND-A-FAILURE`, `TD-C-THE-ACCOUNTS-PAGE-INVENTED-THREE-PEOPLE`, `TD-C-THE-PRIVACY-PAGE-TOLD-YOU-A-BROWSER-HAD-YOUR-CAMERA`, `TD-C-THE-NETWORK-PAGE-LISTED-THREE-ADAPTERS-THIS-SYSTEM-CANNOT-SEE`.
  - [x] `[C]` **Four applications can open a real file, and the reason none of them could is one missing capability** — a follow-on from the fabrication sweep above, and the more important half. Asking *how many other programs are in the state the photo manager was in* gave **115 of the 139 apps with a `main.rs` have no filesystem access at all**: no file picker, no `std::fs`, no `safeio`. The five remaining are all frozen at the *safe* value (autosave on, verify-after-write on), which is luck as much as design: **nothing in the code knows the field is frozen, so nothing chose which way it was stuck.** known-issues.md `TD-C-SETTINGS-THE-PROGRAM-OBEYS-AND-NOTHING-CAN-CHANGE`.

The member was always extracted, so the duplicate was unavoidable from the caller's side and **every gnulib-using C port would have hit it**. `-C codegen-units=4096` in `toolchain/build-sysroot.ps1` restores glibc's one-object-per-module granularity; duplicates went 11 → 0. See `design-decisions.md` §339. **That turned out to be only half the fix (2026-08-20).** The flag buys one member per *module*, and it worked for those four families only because each already happened to be its own module — nothing made that true in general. Writing the check that asserts the property (`scripts/check-libc-shape.py`) immediately found four more members with the identical defect: `asprintf`/`vasprintf` riding with `printf`, `canonicalize_file_name` with `abort`, `getline`/`getdelim`/`fseeko`/`ftello` with `fopen`, and ten string functions (`strndup`, `strverscmp`, `stpcpy`, `stpncpy`, `mempcpy`, `strchrnul`, `memrchr`, `rawmemchr`, `strcasestr`, `strnlen`) with `memcpy` and `strlen`. make missed them only because its `./configure` did not compile in those particular gnulib modules; coreutils and tar would have hit them. All seventeen now sit in one-function inline `mod gnu_<name>` blocks (576 archive members → 593), and the shape is no longer a convention but an assertion: `build-sysroot.ps1` runs the check after assembling `libc.a` and fails the build if it regresses, verified by deliberately rebuilding at `codegen-units=16` and confirming it reports the old shape. See `scripts/cmake-spike/`. This is the first C++ program of real size to reach our libc, and **none of the twenty came from libc++ or the C++ ABI**, which is what design-decisions.md §73 predicted from a toy translation unit. Fourteen of the twenty were the `_l` locale family — POSIX's locale-parameterised spelling of classifiers we already had, and one job rather than fourteen. The other six: `lutimes` (whose plumbing was already here, its `no_follow` argument written for it and named in its doc comment), `in6addr_any`, and `pthread_get/setschedparam` plus `recvmmsg`/`sendmmsg`, the last three of which REFUSE what they cannot deliver rather than succeeding silently. Closing the twenty revealed no second layer. Staged at 22,519,240 bytes `--strip-debug` (274 MB unstripped, which would not fit the 384 MB image). Still deliberately not `[x]`: **shipped is not run** — the same caveat pkgconf and make carry, and cmake leans on the OS harder than either, forking and waiting and opening pipes to compilers. **cmake is the only one of the four whose “shipped is not run” is still true**, and the only one for which no rung was ever requested — now filed as `requests/b-a-cmake-needs-a-ring-3-rung-like-the-other-three.md`, and **lane B's half of that is already done**: five `-P` script fixtures staged in `/usr/share/cmake-selftest` by `scripts/create-ext4-rootfs.sh` — a write, an evaluate, a `file(READ)`, a `file(GLOB)` over a directory, and a `message(FATAL_ERROR)` negative case that asserts both the non-zero exit and the file after it never being written. Every expectation was measured against a real cmake first, which is how the trap was found: `message()` in script mode writes to **stderr**, so a rung modelled on make's — which asserts stdout — would fail forever against a working cmake. The fixtures state their results by writing files instead. It is also the hardest of the four to prove and therefore the most worth proving: pkgconf parses text files, make spawns `/bin/sh`, and cmake does both plus walking directory trees, writing generated build systems and opening pipes to compilers. `gcc` remains the one unmeasured quarter, and its prerequisites (gmp, mpfr, mpc) are not vendored — a dependency gate rather than an effort one.

### 5.1 Linux compatibility layer
- [-] `[D]` Linux syscall translation layer (like FreeBSD's Linuxulator) — broad Linux syscall dispatch already in place (kernel/src/syscall/linux.rs); System V (Linux) initial-process-stack construction added (2026-06-12): new kernel/src/proc/linux_stack.rs builds the argc/argv[]/envp[]/auxv[] stack a Linux `_start` expects (16-byte-aligned %rsp at argc; AT_RANDOM/AT_PAGESZ=4096/AT_PHDR/AT_PHENT/AT_PHNUM/AT_ENTRY/AT_EXECFN/AT_CLKTCK/identity auxv), wired into the AbiMode::Linux branch of spawn_process + exec only (native setup_user_stack untouched, per design-decision #4). Exhaustive boot self_test on the byte layout + an end-to-end test (Linux-tagged ELF that reads argc from [rsp] and exit(argc), verified zombie exit code == argc). The built auxv is now persisted into Linux-ABI PCB state (pcb::linux_saved_auxv, cloned across fork, cleared on exec→native) at spawn/exec time and served back from prctl(PR_GET_AUXV) and /proc/<pid>/auxv (gen_pid_auxv); native processes correctly have no auxv (empty file / 16-byte AT_NULL terminator) per design-decision #4 (2026-06-12). Dynamic-linker (ld.so) load path added (2026-06-12): elf::ElfFile::interp_path() extracts the PT_INTERP path; elf::load_segments_with_bias() maps PT_LOAD at a runtime base; spawn::load_interpreter() reads the interpreter from the VFS, loads it at an ASLR-randomised base drawn from the LINUX_INTERP_BASE=0x0000_7000_0000_0000 window (28 bits of entropy in 16 KiB-page units via apply_aslr_base + rng::next_bounded; interpreter ASLR DONE 2026-06-14, design-decision #20), enters at base+interp.e_entry, and passes Some(base) to the SysV stack builder so ld.so receives AT_BASE (AT_ENTRY stays the executable's e_entry). The PIE main-executable load base is likewise ASLR-randomised from LINUX_PIE_BASE=0x0000_5555_5555_4000 under the same 28-bit policy via choose_exec_load_bias (computed once per spawn/exec, threaded through load_segments_with_bias + the biased entry + AT_ENTRY/AT_PHDR auxv), with a ≥1 TiB headroom invariant below the interpreter window asserted by test_pie_aslr_window — **known-issues.md TD9 fully RESOLVED 2026-06-14**. Defensive fallback (non-UTF-8 path / missing / unreadable / unparseable / unloadable interpreter → enter executable directly) keeps static + native binaries unaffected. Boot self-tests cover interp_path (dynamic/static/empty) and load_interpreter fallbacks (static-ELF + absent-interpreter Ok(None)); end-to-end interpreter EXECUTION deferred until a real glibc/musl ld.so is on disk. **File-backed `mmap` implemented (2026-06-13)** — the #1 blocker for running prebuilt Linux binaries: `ld.so`'s `_dl_map_segments` reserves a load span with a file-backed `MAP_PRIVATE` mmap then overlays each PT_LOAD segment with `MAP_FIXED`, which previously returned ENOSYS. New `linux_file_mmap` (kernel/src/syscall/linux.rs) serves regular-file + memfd maps with an **eager private-copy** model: each 16 KiB frame is `alloc_frame_zeroed`'d, the file bytes are `read_at`-copied in (tail past EOF stays zero, matching Linux page-tail zero-fill), the frame is mapped at prot-derived permissions, and a `VmaKind::Fixed` VMA is registered (so `/proc/<pid>/maps` reflects it and the fault resolver treats a fault there as a bug). `MAP_FIXED` correctly *replaces* an existing mapping via two new helpers — `unmap_user_range` (unmap + refcount-aware free of the old frames) and `pcb::remove_vma_range` (Linux `__split_vma`-style VMA surgery: drops fully-covered VMAs, truncates edge overlaps, splits strict supersets) — which is exactly what ld.so relies on for its segment overlays. Full rollback (unmap+free mapped frames, refund RLIMIT_AS) on any mid-map failure. Writable `MAP_SHARED` returns ENOSYS (no writeback — known-issues.md TD22); read-only `MAP_SHARED` is served as a private copy. VFS-dependent boot self-test `self_test_file_mmap` (throwaway process via pcb::create) verifies a 2-frame file map's content byte-by-byte through a page-table walk, the tail zero-fill, and the MAP_FIXED overlay + VMA split. **MAP_FIXED RLIMIT_AS net-accounting fix (2026-06-13):** the overlay path now charges only the *net* address-space delta — `linux_vma_overlap_bytes` sums the existing-VMA intersection of the target range and that prior charge is subtracted (or released when the new span is smaller), so ld.so reserving a span then overlaying each segment with MAP_FIXED no longer ~2x over-counts; the self-test asserts RLIMIT_AS == length_aligned after the map and unchanged after the single-frame overlay. **Ring-3 end-to-end test added (2026-06-13):** `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_file_mmap` spawns a real Linux-ABI process (hand-assembled `elf::build_linux_mmap_test_elf`) that itself issues `open(2)`+`mmap(2)`, reads a byte from the *second* 16 KiB frame of the mapping, and `exit`s with it — proving the whole syscall path (fd install via open's `require_cap_type(File,READ)` gate, `mmap` dispatch with a live `caller_pid`, ring-3 readability, multi-frame file content delivery) works, not just the kernel-context helper. **Real `brk`/`sbrk` heap implemented (2026-06-14)** — `sys_brk` (kernel/src/syscall/linux.rs) was a no-op stub that echoed the requested break while mapping nothing (a latent ring-3 SIGSEGV for any glibc program whose malloc used the brk fast path). Now a real per-process demand-paged heap: new `brk_start`/`brk_current` PCB fields (inherited across fork as a CoW heap, recomputed from the new image's page-aligned `elf::image_end` on exec for Linux images / cleared for native), a single `VmaKind::Brk` VMA labelled `[heap]` in /proc/maps that faults zero-filled like Anonymous, grow that charges RLIMIT_AS for the full added virtual span up-front (committed-by-default) and enforces RLIMIT_DATA, shrink that unmaps+frees faulted frames and refunds the charge, an image-dependent ceiling (`USER_MMAP_BASE` for low ET_EXEC, `LINUX_INTERP_BASE` for high PIE) plus a VMA-overlap guard, and Linux's return-the-unchanged-break-on-any-failure contract (so glibc's `__sbrk` falls back to mmap). Tests: pure `self_test_brk_logic` (brk_round_up boundary/overflow + brk_ceiling ET_EXEC/PIE) and ring-3 `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_brk` (real process queries break, grows 32 KiB, writes/reads the second heap frame, exits 0x6D). The heap floor is ASLR'd via `spawn::choose_brk_start` (Linux `arch_randomize_brk`, 13 bits of entropy / 128 MiB max gap at 16 KiB pages, matching Linux's position count per design-decisions #20/#21; covered by `test_brk_aslr_gap`). **`madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` reclaim implemented (2026-06-14)** — `sys_madvise` previously accepted MADV_DONTNEED/MADV_FREE/MADV_DONTNEED_LOCKED but never freed anything (documented limitation pending VMA tracking), so long-running glibc/jemalloc/tcmalloc processes that `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` freed arenas grew RSS unbounded. Now that the brk/mmap VMA layer exists, those hints free the resident frames backing anonymous-class pages (Anonymous/Stack/Brk VMAs) in the range via `madvise_reclaim` (reuses `unmap_user_range`: refcount-aware free + per-page TLB invalidation; VMA + RLIMIT_AS reservation preserved so the mapping stays valid and a later access zero-fills via the fault resolver — exactly Linux's anonymous DONTNEED contract; only whole 16 KiB frames fully inside the 4 KiB-ABI request are dropped; file-backed/fixed maps keep the lenient no-op). Tested by boot self-test `self_test_madvise_dontneed` (faults 2 anon frames, stamps a sentinel, reclaims, asserts PTEs cleared + VMA persists + re-fault reads zero). A coverage audit confirmed **every defined Linux syscall number is dispatched** (the flat `dispatch_linux` match + the frame-aware `dispatch_linux_with_frame` for fork/vfork/clone); remaining `ENOSYS` returns are deliberate (io_uring/AIO/fanotify with proper validation gates). **Path Z END-TO-END ACHIEVED (2026-06-15):** a real prebuilt **dynamically-linked glibc** binary (`/bin/hello`) now runs the *complete* startup — ring-3 `ld.so` maps `libc.so.6`, applies relocations, sets up TLS, and `__libc_start_main → main → exit_group(42)` — driven from boot by `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc` (verdict: `REAL glibc dynamic execution (ring 3: ld.so mapped libc.so.6, relocated, set up TLS, __libc_start_main → main → exit(42)): OK`; three BOOT_OK cycles). The real-glibc **output** path is proven too (2026-06-15): `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_stdio` runs a second prebuilt binary (`/bin/stdio`, `printf("…%d\n", 1234)`) with its fd 1 redirected from the console to a capture file (via new `pcb::linux_fd_install_at`), drives glibc's full-buffered stdio → exit-time `write(2)` flush, and asserts the captured 26 bytes match exactly — the gate for any glibc program that produces output. The real-glibc **argv/env/stdin/heap** paths are proven too (2026-06-15): `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_full` runs a third prebuilt binary (`/bin/full`) that sums `argv[]` lengths, reads `getenv("SLATE_TAG")`, `fgets()`-es a line from a redirected fd 0, and runs 64 rounds of mixed small (brk-arena) + large (>128 KiB, mmap-backed) `malloc`/`free` touching every page; with fd 0 fed a known input file and fd 1 redirected to a capture file, the test asserts the exact deterministic output line and `exit(11)` — proving the kernel-built argv vector, envp delivery, the glibc *input* path (`fstat(0)` buffering + `read(2)`), and the brk+mmap heap under genuine glibc allocator pressure. The final blocker was **16 KiB-frame vs. 4 KiB-ABI mismatch**: standard x86-64 glibc links with `max-page-size=0x1000`, so `ld.so` overlays adjacent library segments with *different* permissions (R-- rodata, RW- data) that share one 16 KiB physical frame and uses 4 KiB-aligned `MAP_FIXED`/`mprotect` (e.g. RELRO `mprotect(0x…203000, 0x4000, PROT_READ)`). Resolved by making the memory subsystem **4 KiB-sub-frame-granular** while keeping the 16 KiB frame as the allocation/RSS/rmap/reclaim unit: (1) per-subpage demand faulting — `pcb::resolve_subpaged_fault` resolves each 4 KiB subpage of a straddling frame with its own PTE permissions/file-backing via `map_4k_if_absent`, plus `change_flags_4k`/`is_hw_page_aligned` page-table primitives; (2) 4 KiB-granular anonymous `MAP_FIXED` (`linux_anon_mmap_fixed` + a `sys_mmap` fixed-dispatch path, fixing the bss zero-fill overlay); (3) 4 KiB-granular `mprotect` (`mprotect_validate_args`/`sys_mprotect` now gate + step on `HW_PAGE_SIZE` and flip a single PTE via `change_flags_4k`, fixing RELRO); (4) per-subpage ELF segment loading (two-pass `elf.rs` loader maps each 16 KiB frame with the union of its overlapping segments' permissions via `map_frame_subpages`, preserving W^X). **`mprotect` is now VMA-aware (2026-06-15, known-issues TD27 FIXED):** `sys_mprotect` calls `pcb::protect_vma_range`, which performs per-subpage VMA surgery (`vma_subrange` splits VMAs at 4 KiB boundaries and recomputes WRITABLE/NO_EXECUTE, adjusting FileBacked `file_offset`s) so the VMA flag set tracks the live permission — a RELRO page reclaimed under memory pressure and re-faulted now restores the *read-only* permission the `mprotect` established, not the old writable VMA permission. Coverage is validated Linux-style *before* any mutation: `vma_coverage_gaps` plus a present-PTE check accepts the eagerly-mapped (VMA-less but PTE-present) PIE/RELRO segments while still returning ENOMEM on a genuine hole. **Path Z Part 4 — real glibc pthread (clone3 + CLONE_SETTLS TLS + futex) ACHIEVED (2026-06-15):** `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_pthread` runs a fourth prebuilt binary (`/bin/pthread`) that spawns 4 worker threads via `pthread_create` (glibc `clone3` with `CLONE_VM|FS|FILES|SIGHAND|THREAD|SETTLS|PARENT_SETTID|CHILD_CLEARTID`, each thread's stack demand-paged through the VMA fault resolver after glibc's pre-touch `mprotect`), runs 40000 `pthread_mutex` ops across them (uncontended CAS fast path + contended `futex_wait`/`futex_wake`), and `pthread_join`s all four (each join blocks on the child-tid futex zeroed-and-woken by CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID on thread exit) — asserting the deterministic `SLATE_GLIBC_PTHREAD_OK counter=40000 joinsum=10\n` output and `exit(13)`. The final blocker was the **futex-wait Linux-ABI return-value convention**: Slate's native futex handlers return `Ok(1)` for blocked-and-woken / `Ok(0)` for value-mismatch, but Linux `FUTEX_WAIT*` must return `0` on wake / `-EAGAIN` on mismatch / `-ETIMEDOUT` on timeout, and glibc calls `futex_fatal_error()` (aborting) on any other value. Fixed by `linux_from_futex_wait` (maps native `1→0`, `0→-EAGAIN`, negative errors via `linux_from_native`), applied to FUTEX_WAIT / FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET / futex2_wait / waitv. **Path Z Part 5 — real glibc signals (byte-exact Linux `rt_sigframe`) ACHIEVED (2026-06-15):** unmodified glibc binaries can now install `SA_SIGINFO` handlers and return from them. Signal delivery for `AbiMode::Linux` processes branches (in `handlers.rs::deliver_pending_signal` → new `deliver_linux_signal`) away from the native SEH-style `SignalContext` trampoline into `linux::build_linux_rt_frame`, which constructs a byte-exact Linux `struct rt_sigframe` (256B `sigcontext_64` + 304B `ucontext` + 128B `siginfo`, in `kernel/src/proc/linux_sigframe.rs`) on the user stack with Linux's `align_sigframe` rule (`sp = round_down(sp - size, 16) - 8`, so the ucontext is 16-aligned), enters the handler with `rdi=signo, rsi=&siginfo, rdx=&ucontext, rsp=&pretcode, rip=sa_handler`, and wires `pretcode = sa_restorer` so the handler's `ret` jumps to glibc's `__restore_rt` (`mov $15,%rax; syscall` → `rt_sigreturn`). `linux_rt_sigreturn` (rewritten) restores all GPRs/rip/rsp from the user ucontext's `uc_mcontext`, **sanitizes the attacker-controlled RFLAGS** (keeps only `SIGRETURN_RFLAGS_USER_MASK=0x0024_0DD5`, force-sets `SIGRETURN_RFLAGS_FORCED=0x202` = IF+reserved bit, dropping IOPL/NT/VM), and restores the saved signal mask. Per-signal Linux disposition (`linux_disposition` → Handler/Ignore/Default over the per-process `LinuxSigaction` table) honours `SA_NODEFER`/`SA_RESETHAND`/`sa_mask` blocking semantics; Default falls through to terminate/stop/ignore/continue. Proven in ring 3 by `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_signal` (a fifth prebuilt binary `/bin/signal` installs an `SA_SIGINFO` SIGUSR1 handler, `raise()`s it, reads the delivered `siginfo`, resumes via `rt_sigreturn`, asserts `si_code == SI_TKILL` and `si_pid == getpid()`, prints `SLATE_GLIBC_SIGNAL_OK signo=10 code=-6 self=1` and `exit(17)` — captured bytes asserted exactly). **Sender-faithful `siginfo` (2026-06-15, known-issues TD29 RESOLVED):** `SignalState` (`kernel/src/proc/signal.rs`) now carries a per-signal `Option<SigInfo>` array co-located under the pending-bitmap lock, recorded on the clear→set transition (Linux standard-signal first-wins coalescing) and taken at delivery, so the `siginfo` handed to an `SA_SIGINFO` handler reports the correct sender class — `kill(2)`→`SI_USER`+sender pid/uid, `tkill`/`tgkill` (`raise`/`pthread_kill`)→`SI_TKILL`+sender pid, timer expiry (SIGALRM)→`SI_KERNEL`. Threaded through the post funnel (`kill_common`/`sys_signal_send_with_code`→`classify_post_info`→`set_pending_info`) and consumed by `build_linux_rt_frame`; covered by the `siginfo record/deliver/coalesce` unit self-test (13 signal tests). **Path Z Part 5b — synchronous fault → Linux signal with faithful `si_addr`/`si_code` (2026-06-16):** a CPU fault taken by an `AbiMode::Linux` process with an installed handler is now delivered as a real Linux signal carrying a fault-specific `siginfo`. The delicate `rt_sigframe`-building logic is extracted into a shared emitter `emit_linux_rt_frame(pid, sig, act, regs: &LinuxTrapRegs, siginfo) -> Option<RtFrameEntry>` (`kernel/src/syscall/linux.rs`) that takes a neutral register snapshot, so it is reused by both the async syscall-return path (`build_linux_rt_frame`, snapshot from the `SyscallFrame`) and the synchronous fault path (`try_deliver_linux_fault_signal`, `kernel/src/idt.rs`, snapshot read out of the `InterruptStackFrame` + `SavedRegisters` via `read_volatile` raw-pointer discipline — never forming an `&mut` from the ISR frame). `linux_fault_mapping` classifies the trap vector → `(signo, si_code)` (`#DE`→`SIGFPE`/`FPE_INTDIV`, `#OF`→`SIGFPE`/`FPE_INTOVF`, `#UD`→`SIGILL`/`ILL_ILLOPN`, `#MF`/`#XM`→`SIGFPE`/`FPE_FLTINV`, `#AC`→`SIGBUS`/`BUS_ADRALN`, `#BR`/`#NP`/`#SS`/`#GP`→`SIGSEGV`/`SI_KERNEL`; `si_addr` = faulting RIP for these). `#PF` is handled in `handle_page_fault`, which sets `si_addr = CR2` and `si_code = SEGV_ACCERR` (present bit set → protection) or `SEGV_MAPERR` (not mapped). The emitter does **not** re-arm on a frame-build failure — the fault caller terminates instead (resuming would immediately re-fault). Native processes keep the SEH-style `SignalContext` trampoline (design-decision #4). Proven in ring 3 by `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_fault` (a sixth prebuilt binary `/bin/fault` stores to an unmapped `0xDEAD000`, taking a real `#PF` that enters an unmodified glibc `SA_SIGINFO` SIGSEGV handler reading `si_signo==11`/`si_code==SEGV_MAPERR(1)`/`si_addr==0xdead000` and `siglongjmp`ing out, printing `SLATE_GLIBC_FAULT_OK signo=11 code=1 addr=0xdead000` and `exit(19)` — captured 52 bytes asserted exactly, boot test PASSED). **Path Z Part 5c — `SI_QUEUE` `si_value` payload (2026-06-16):** `rt_sigqueueinfo(2)`, `rt_tgsigqueueinfo(2)` and `pidfd_send_signal(2)` now read the user-supplied `siginfo` (`read_user_siginfo_payload`, SMAP-safe `copy_from_user`), carry `si_code` + the 8-byte `si_value` union onto the pending signal, and stamp them into the delivered `siginfo_t` at the ABI offset (struct +24) via the new `LinuxSiginfo::queue(...)` builder (`build_linux_rt_frame` branches to it when `si_code == SI_QUEUE`). The kill funnel was refactored into shared `kill_common_value` / `tgkill_common_value` / `sys_signal_send_with_info(args, si_code, value)` cores so all gate ordering (EFAULT → forging-EPERM → ESRCH-before-EINVAL → authority) is reused and only the final post stamps the payload; Linux's `do_rt_sigqueueinfo` forging gate (`(si_code >= 0 || si_code == SI_TKILL) && caller != target → EPERM`) is enforced on all three queued-signal entry points, with the recorded `si_pid`/`si_uid` always the *real caller* (unforgeable). Proven in ring 3 by `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_sigqueue` (a seventh prebuilt binary `/bin/sigqueue` `sigqueue(getpid(), SIGUSR1, {.sival_int=0x12345678})`s itself; the `SA_SIGINFO` handler reads `si_code==SI_QUEUE(-1)`, `si_value.sival_int==0x12345678`, `si_pid==getpid()`, printing `SLATE_GLIBC_SIGQUEUE_OK signo=10 code=-1 value=0x12345678 self=1` and `exit(23)` — captured 65 bytes asserted exactly, boot test PASSED) plus in-kernel forging-gate (EPERM) and SI_QUEUE-bypass (ESRCH-before-EINVAL) assertions. **Path Z Part 6 — real glibc `fork()`+`execl()`+`waitpid()` of a real glibc child ACHIEVED (2026-06-16):** an unmodified glibc binary can now `fork()` (glibc's `arch_fork` issues `clone(SIGCHLD|CLONE_CHILD_SETTID|CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID, stack=0, ptid=0, ctid=&THREAD_SELF->tid, tls=0)`), have the child `execl()` a *different* real glibc binary (re-running `ld.so`/`libc.so.6` startup in the CoW child image), and reap it via `waitpid()`→`wait4`. The blocker was the Linux `clone()` fork-equivalent path (`linux_clone_inner`, `kernel/src/syscall/linux.rs`) rejecting glibc's fork with `-ENOSYS` because its reject mask lumped the TID-notification bits (`CLONE_CHILD_SETTID`/`CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID`/`CLONE_PARENT_SETTID`) in with the genuinely-unsupported partial-resource-share bits. Fixed by narrowing the fork-path reject mask to `FORK_REJECTED_SHARE_BITS` (CLONE_VM/FS/FILES/SIGHAND/THREAD/SYSVSEM/SETTLS only) and **honouring the TID-notification bits across a CoW fork**: `fork::ForkCloneTid` threads the bits into `fork::fork_process_clone`, which writes `CLONE_PARENT_SETTID` (child's task-id → parent's `ptid`, in the parent's still-active address space), registers `CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID` (`register_clear_child_tid(child_task_id, ctid)` so the child-tid futex is zeroed-and-woken on the child's exit — glibc's own `fork()` relies on this internally), and defers `CLONE_CHILD_SETTID` to a child-context write inside `fork_child_trampoline` (the new `ForkChildImage` carries the `settid_ptr`) — the write *must* run in the child's CoW address space, since doing it from the parent would trip copy-on-write and the value would never reach the child. The forked child's `execve` keeps the same task-id, so glibc startup's `set_tid_address(&new_tcb.tid)` re-registers the clear-child-tid slot at a valid address in the new image (no execve-clear needed). Proven in ring 3 by `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_forkexec` (an eighth prebuilt binary `/bin/forkexec` `fork()`s, the child `execl("/bin/hello")` — the silent real-glibc binary that exits 42 — and the parent `waitpid()`s and prints `SLATE_GLIBC_FORKEXEC_OK childexit=42` returning 27; captured 37 bytes asserted exactly, boot test PASSED). This is the foundation for a real shell. **Path Z Part 7 — real glibc `pipe()`+`fork()`+`dup2()`+`execl()`+`read()`-to-EOF+`waitpid()` (the `cmd1 | cmd2` shell primitive) ACHIEVED (2026-06-16):** two new prebuilt glibc binaries — `/bin/emit` (writes `"SLATE_PIPE_BODY\n"` to fd 1) and `/bin/pipe` (`pipe(2)`→`fork(2)`; the child `dup2`s the write end onto fd 1, closes the raw ends, and `execl`s `/bin/emit`; the parent closes the write end, `read`s the pipe to EOF, `waitpid`s the child, and `printf`s what it read) — prove the full pipeline plumbing a shell builds: (a) pipe-fd inheritance across the CoW fork, (b) `dup2` redirection, (c) open fds surviving `execve` into a fresh glibc image, and (d) pipe EOF arriving once every write end (parent's + the exec'd child's) is closed. **Two latent kernel correctness bugs were found and fixed in the process: (1) fd-bearing resources were closed at *reap* (`destroy`) instead of at *exit* (zombie), causing a pipe deadlock** — a parent blocked in `read()` waiting for EOF could never get it, because EOF requires the child's inherited pipe write end to close, but that close only happened when the parent reaped the child, and the parent couldn't reach `waitpid()` until EOF (classic deadlock). Fixed by `pcb::exit_close_fds(pid)`, called from `thread::on_thread_exit` at the zombie transition, which closes every `ipc_handle` + unclaimed initial fd the moment the process exits — matching Linux's `exit_files()` in `do_exit` (a process's open file descriptions close when it *exits*, not when its parent reaps it). `destroy_process_resources` still runs the same teardown for the force-kill / never-zombied path (the slices are empty by then on the normal path), so no double-close and no leak. **(2) `on_thread_exit_hook` dereferenced user pointers (PI-futex owner walk, robust-list, `clear_child_tid`) unconditionally, panicking with a page fault when the cleanup ran cross-address-space** — e.g. a boot self-test reaping a glibc process from task 0's (boot) address space. Fixed with an AS-active guard: the user-memory operations now run only when the active CR3 equals the dying task's process PML4 (`page_table::active_pml4_phys() == pcb::get_pml4(owner_process(task_id))`); the in-kernel map removals (`ROBUST_LIST`/`RSEQ`/`CLEAR_CHILD_TID`) always run. (See known-issues.md F16, F17.) Proven in ring 3 by `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_pipe` (captured 46 bytes `SLATE_GLIBC_PIPE_OK n=16 body=SLATE_PIPE_BODY\n` == expected, `exit(29)`, boot test PASSED). **Path Z Part 8 — real glibc program-driven `cmd > file` output redirection ACHIEVED (2026-06-16):** a ninth prebuilt glibc binary (`/bin/redir`) performs its *own* shell-style output redirection entirely from ring 3 — `open("/redir-out.txt", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0644)`, `dup2(fd, 1)` (redirecting stdout onto the just-opened file), `close(fd)`, then `printf("SLATE_GLIBC_REDIR_OK marker=%d\n", 4242)` whose glibc full-buffered stdio flushes to the program's own file at exit. This proves the redirection direction a shell builds for `> file` (vs Part 7's `dup2` onto a *pipe*): (a) ring-3 `open(2)` with `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC` creating a fresh file through `translate_open_flags`→VFS, (b) `dup2(2)` of a self-`open()`ed **File** handle onto fd 1 — exercising the displaced-console-fd close path (the original fd-1 console handle's refcount is correctly dropped when overwritten via `sys_dup2_impl`→`close_handle`→`sys_fs_close`→`deregister_ipc_handle`), and (c) glibc's exit-time stdio flush landing in the redirected file. `proc::spawn::self_test_linux_real_glibc_redir` spawns `/bin/redir` with **no fd injection** (the program opens its own file), polls for the zombie, reads `/redir-out.txt` back via `Vfs::read_file`, and asserts `exit(31)` and the captured 33 bytes (`SLATE_GLIBC_REDIR_OK marker=4242\n`) match exactly (boot test PASSED). **Path Z Part 9 — real glibc program-driven `cmd < file` input redirection ACHIEVED (2026-06-16):** the mirror image of Part 8 — a tenth prebuilt glibc binary (`/bin/redirin`) performs its *own* shell-style *input* redirection from ring 3 — `open("/redir-in.txt", O_RDONLY)`, `dup2(fd, 0)` (redirecting stdin from the just-opened file), `close(fd)`, then `fgets(buf, …, stdin)` reading a line through glibc's buffered input path. With **no fd injection** (only a `File READ|WRITE` cap), the test reads `/dash-pipe-out.txt` back and asserts `exit(0)` and the exact 5 bytes `n=16\n`. **A latent kernel CoW correctness bug was found and fixed (known-issues.md F18):** a per-16 KiB-frame refcount vs per-4 KiB-PTE CoW-resolution granularity mismatch double-freed a still-shared frame, crashing the *parent* dash with a #GP at glibc `wait4`'s errno store (`mov %eax,%fs:(%rdx)`) — but only on the `wait4` error path, which is why the single-fork Part 11 never hit it. The ELF loader packs a read-only segment tail and a writable segment head into one 16 KiB frame; a forked child resolving the writable CoW sub-PTE decremented the frame's refcount once *while still mapping it via the read-only sub-PTE*, then double-decremented it at exec teardown (which freed per group keyed on only the base PTE), driving a parent-shared frame to refcount 0 → reuse → `.got` errno-slot corruption → garbage `%rdx` → #GP. Fixed by making CoW refcounting consistent across `cow::resolve_cow_fault`, `cow::clone_frame_group`, and `page_table::clear_user_address_space` on one invariant — *each address space holds exactly one refcount on each **distinct** 16 KiB frame its group's sub-PTEs reference*: resolve drops the old frame's reference only when no sub-PTE of the group still points into it; clone increments once per distinct frame among present siblings; teardown inspects all four sub-PTEs and frees each distinct frame once. Path Z Part 20 — real dash background job + `wait` builtin (2026-06-16): `dash -c '/bin/emit > /bg-out.txt & wait'` now runs end-to-end in ring 3. dash forks /bin/emit as an asynchronous job (redirecting its stdout to the file), returns to the prompt, then the `wait` builtin blocks until the child is reaped. This exercised the real dash job-control path: dash arms a SIGCHLD handler, calls `waitpid(WNOHANG)`, and `rt_sigsuspend`s until SIGCHLD wakes it (the synchronous pipe/loop/cmdsub parts use blocking waitpid and never needed SIGCHLD). Two kernel gaps were fixed to make this work, both proper fixes: (1) SIGCHLD is now posted to the parent process when a child becomes a zombie (`proc/thread.rs` `on_thread_exit`) — via the Linux-ABI disposition path for Linux parents (`set_pending_info`, delivered through `deliver_linux_signal`→`linux_disposition`) and `classify_post` for native parents; and (2) `sys_rt_sigsuspend` is no longer a stub returning EINTR immediately (which livelocked dash into a busy-spin that starved the boot thread) but a real park loop modeled on `sys_pause`: it installs the temporary mask, blocks on the signalfd wait-queue until a signal deliverable under that mask arrives, and restores the original mask correctly via a Linux saved_sigmask/TIF_RESTORE_SIGMASK mechanism (`emit_linux_rt_frame` writes the saved pre-suspend mask into `uc_sigmask` so `rt_sigreturn` restores it; the no-handler tail of `deliver_linux_signal` restores it directly). Path Z Part 23 — real dash relative-path open after cd (cwd resolution fix) (2026-06-16): `dash -c 'cd /reltest && echo RELOK > relfile.txt'` now correctly creates `/reltest/relfile.txt` (cwd-relative), not `/relfile.txt` (root). The fix resolves relative paths against `pcb::get_cwd(caller)` at the Linux ABI boundary using the existing `canonicalize_path` helper: `open_common` canonicalises then opens via a new kernel-string `handlers::fs_open_kernel_path`, and `resolve_at_path` canonicalises its AT_FDCWD/absolute result. Kernel context and the native ABI are unchanged (cwd falls back to `/`). Self-test asserts the file landed cwd-relative and NOT at root, reads back 6 bytes == expected, exit 0. Path Z Part 24 — path-based stat now does real VFS lookups (stat-stub fix) (2026-06-16): the Linux-ABI stat/lstat/newfstatat/statx syscalls all unconditionally returned ENOENT for path lookups (stale no-file skeleton-FS assumption), so any program that stat'd a path before opening it — e.g. dash's `[ -f FILE ]` test predicate, `ls`, configure probes — saw every file as missing even though the VFS now holds real files. Fix: stat_path_common (shared by stat follow / lstat no-follow) and the non-empty-path branches of newfstatat/statx now canonicalise the path against the caller's cwd and call Vfs::metadata (follow) / Vfs::lmetadata (no-follow) via the new stat_meta_for_path + fill_stat_from_meta / fill_statx_from_meta helpers, which map EntryType→S_IF* bits (default perms 0o755/0o777/0o644 when the FS reports none) and backfill 0 timestamps with the current realtime clock. Statbuf pointer gates are deferred until after a successful lookup, matching Linux's getname/filename_lookup-before-cp_new_stat ordering. Kernel context (caller_pid().is_none()) still returns ENOENT, preserving the batch-488 syscall-fidelity self-tests. Path Z Part 27 — symlink()/readlink() syscalls now do real VFS work (symlink/readlink stub fix) (2026-06-16): the Linux-ABI symlink/symlinkat syscalls were stale stubs returning EROFS and readlink/readlinkat returned EINVAL unconditionally, even though the VFS is fully writable and supports symlinks — so no ring-3 program could create or resolve a symlink. Fix: sys_symlink/sys_symlinkat share a new symlink_common back-end that stores the target verbatim (a symlink may dangle / be relative, so the target is NOT resolved or canonicalised) while resolving the linkpath against the caller's cwd/newdirfd via resolve_at_path, requires a File-WRITE capability (require_fs_write), and calls Vfs::symlink; sys_readlink/sys_readlinkat share a new do_readlink_copy back-end that calls Vfs::readlink and copies min(target_len, bufsiz) bytes with NO trailing NUL, returning the byte count (Linux do_readlinkat contract), validating the user buffer only after the dentry is confirmed to be a symlink (NotFound→ENOENT, InvalidArgument→EINVAL/"not a symlink"). Kernel context (caller_pid().is_none()) preserves the prior EROFS/EINVAL terminals the batch-478/487 syscall-fidelity self-tests assert; only ring-3 callers do real VFS work. Self-test: a hand-built raw-syscall Linux-ABI ELF (build_linux_symlink_readlink_test_elf) calls symlink("Z", "/sl-rl-link") then readlink("/sl-rl-link", buf, 64) from ring 3 and asserts the call returned exactly 1 byte == 'Z'; self-diagnosing exit sentinels 0xB1/0xB3/0xB4. The harness pre-removes the link path (no EEXIST) and, after the process exits 0, independently confirms kernel-side via Vfs::readlink that the created link resolves to "Z". (Raw ELF rather than dash because dash has no `ln` builtin and cannot invoke symlink(2)/readlink(2) directly.) Path Z Part 28 — link()/linkat() syscalls now create real hard links (link stub fix) (2026-06-16): the Linux-ABI link/linkat syscalls were stale stubs returning EROFS after their argument gates, even though the VFS supports hard links (Vfs::link). Fix: sys_link/sys_linkat share a new link_common back-end that resolves both the existing (oldpath) and new (newpath) names against the caller's cwd/dirfds via resolve_at_path, requires a File-WRITE capability (require_fs_write), and calls Vfs::link (which follows symlinks in oldpath and rejects cross-mount links). Kernel context (caller_pid().is_none()) preserves the EROFS terminal the batch-481 syscall-fidelity self-test asserts. Fidelity note: plain link(2) should NOT follow a symlink oldpath and linkat follows only with AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW, but Vfs::link always follows — so the rare symlink-as-oldpath case links the target instead (documented in known-issues B-SYM1). Self-test: a hand-built raw-syscall Linux-ABI ELF (build_linux_link_test_elf) calls link("/mnt/lnk-src", "/mnt/lnk-dst") then open("/mnt/lnk-dst", O_RDONLY)+read one byte from ring 3 and asserts it is 'L' (the byte the harness pre-wrote to /mnt/lnk-src); self-diagnosing exit sentinels 0xC1/0xC2/0xC3/0xC4. After the process exits 0, the harness independently confirms kernel-side via Vfs::read_file that /mnt/lnk-dst reads back "L". The test runs on the ext4 mount at /mnt (not the memfs root): memfs stores file data inline in by-value tree nodes and cannot share an inode between two names, so it correctly reports unsupported — Linux likewise returns EPERM for FSes without hard-link support; ext4 implements real hard links. memfs hard-link support would need an inode-table refactor and is deferred (documented in known-issues B-SYM1). Path Z Part 29 — utimensat()/utimes()/utime() now apply file timestamps (timestamp-stub fix) (2026-06-16): the Linux-ABI utimensat/utimes/utime family were stale stubs returning EROFS after their Linux-faithful input-shape gate ladders (batch 489), even though Vfs::set_times is implemented by memfs/ext4/fat — so no ring-3 program could update a file's atime/mtime (touch, make target stamping, tar -x mtime restore, configure probes). Fix: for ring-3 callers each handler resolves the target (resolve_at_path against the caller's cwd/dirfd; utimensat with a NULL pathname resolves the open file behind dirfd via handle_path), translates the parsed timespec/timeval/utimbuf into ns-since-epoch (UTIME_NOW→clock_realtime, UTIME_OMIT/NULL-field→leave-unchanged, otherwise sec*1e9[+sub-second]), requires a File-WRITE capability, and calls Vfs::set_times. Kernel context (caller_pid().is_none()) preserves the EROFS terminal the batch-489 syscall-fidelity self-tests assert. Fidelity gaps (minor, documented in known-issues B-UTIME1): Vfs::set_times always follows symlinks so utimensat's AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW is a no-op, and the Timestamp=u64 VFS API overloads 0 as the leave-unchanged sentinel so setting a field to exactly the Unix epoch / a pre-epoch instant is treated as leave-unchanged. Self-test: a hand-built raw-syscall Linux-ABI ELF (build_linux_utimensat_test_elf) calls utimensat(AT_FDCWD, "/utimensat-test", {atime=1.6e9 s, mtime=1.5e9 s}, 0) from ring 3 (self-diagnosing exit sentinel 0xD1); the harness stages the file on the memfs root (memfs implements set_times, unlike hard links) and, after the process exits 0, independently asserts the kernel-side Vfs::metadata reports accessed_ns==1.6e18 and modified_ns==1.5e18 exactly. Path Z Part 30 — chmod()/fchmod()/fchmodat()/chown()/lchown()/fchown()/fchownat() now mutate file metadata (chmod/chown stub fix) (2026-06-16): the entire Linux-ABI chmod/chown family were stale stubs returning EROFS after their (batch-483/484) input-shape gates, even though the VFS tracks Unix mode bits and uid/gid and implements Vfs::set_permissions / Vfs::set_owner across memfs/ext4/fat — so no ring-3 program could chmod +x, install -m, or restore perms/owner from a tar. Fix: for ring-3 callers each handler resolves the target (resolve_at_path for path variants against the caller's cwd/dirfd; handle_path on the open file for the fchmod/fchown fd variants and the fchownat(AT_EMPTY_PATH) form), requires a File-WRITE capability, and calls Vfs::set_permissions (mode masked to 0o7777 via a shared chmod_apply) or Vfs::set_owner (uid/gid narrowed to 32 bits via a shared chown_apply; the (uid_t)-1/(gid_t)-1 leave-unchanged sentinels are honoured by Vfs::set_owner). Kernel context (caller_pid().is_none()) preserves the EROFS terminal the fidelity self-tests assert; fchmod/fchown on a non-file fd (pipe/console) return EINVAL. Fidelity gaps (minor, known-issues B-CHOWN1): lchown / fchownat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) still follow the final symlink (set_owner always follows), and chmod/chown are gated on the generic File-WRITE capability rather than a dedicated CAP_CHOWN/CAP_FOWNER. Self-test: a hand-built raw-syscall ELF (build_linux_chmod_chown_test_elf) calls chmod("/chmod-chown-test", 0o640) then chown(path, 1234, 5678) from ring 3 (sentinels 0xE1/0xE2); the harness stages the file on the memfs root and, after the process exits 0, independently asserts Vfs::metadata reports permissions==0o640, uid==1234, gid==5678. Part 31 — truncate() and ftruncate() now resize files for ring-3 callers (truncate/ftruncate stub fix; known-issues B-TRUNC1). Both syscalls previously ran their full input-shape gate ladders (EINVAL on negative length, EFAULT/ENOENT on bad/empty/missing paths, EISDIR on directories, EINVAL on non-regular inodes and on a read-only fd via the FMODE_WRITE check) and then hard-coded EROFS for a confirmed regular file, even though Vfs::truncate is implemented across memfs/ext4/fat. Now, for ring-3 callers, sys_truncate (after its real Vfs::stat triage confirms a regular file) and sys_ftruncate's File arm enforce RLIMIT_FSIZE (EFBIG on a grow past the soft limit → the check returns to its proper Linux position now that mounts are writable, between the FMODE_WRITE/mnt_want_write gate and do_truncate), require a File-WRITE capability, resolve the target (canonicalize_path for the path variant, handle_path on the open fd for ftruncate), and call Vfs::truncate (grow-with-zeros or shrink). Kernel context keeps the EROFS terminal (gated on caller_pid().is_none()), so the batch-447/448 fidelity self-tests still pass. Self-test (Path Z Part 31, self_test_linux_truncate): a hand-built raw-syscall ELF (build_linux_truncate_test_elf) shrinks /truncate-test to 4 bytes via the path syscall, then open(O_RDWR)+ftruncate(fd, 10) grows it (sentinels 0xF1/0xF2/0xF3); the harness stages a 16-byte file on the memfs root and, after the process exits 0, independently asserts the readback is exactly 10 bytes with the leading 4 preserved ('A') and the grown tail zero-filled. Part 32 — fchmodat2() (syscall #452, the 4-arg flags-aware chmod) now mutates file metadata for ring-3 callers (fchmodat2 stub fix; known-issues B-CHOWN1 follow-up). It was a separate EROFS stub missed by the Part 30 chmod/chown pass; it is now wired in the same idiom as sys_fchownat. AT_EMPTY_PATH resolves dirfd to its backing path (AT_FDCWD → cwd, else an open File fd via handle_path) then chmod_apply; the non-AT_EMPTY_PATH branch keeps the empty-path → ENOENT getname discrimination, then (for ring-3 callers) resolve_at_path + chmod_apply (real Vfs::set_permissions). Kernel context keeps the EROFS terminal, so the batch-485 fidelity self-test stays green. Fidelity gap (minor, known-issues B-CHOWN1): AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW is ignored (set_permissions always follows the final symlink). Self-test (Path Z Part 32, self_test_linux_fchmodat2): a hand-built raw-syscall ELF (build_linux_fchmodat2_emptypath_test_elf) open(O_RDWR)s /fchmodat2-test and calls fchmodat2(fd, "", 0o600, AT_EMPTY_PATH) from ring 3 (sentinels 0xE5/0xE6); the harness stages the file on the memfs root and, after the process exits 0, independently asserts Vfs::metadata reports permissions==0o600. Path Z Part 33 (fallocate real allocate — syscall #285): wired sys_fallocate from the stale EOPNOTSUPP terminal ("Our VFS doesn't expose fallocate") to the real VFS for ring-3 callers, completing the FS-write line. The full Linux gate ladder (fd validation → offset/len bounds → unknown-mode-bits → PUNCH|ZERO mutual exclusion → PUNCH-needs-KEEP_SIZE → COLLAPSE/INSERT/UNSHARE exclusivity → FMODE_WRITE) is unchanged; after it, ring-3 callers now classify the fd's inode kind (Linux's FIFO→ESPIPE / non-regular→ENODEV gates) and dispatch the two well-defined allocate modes: mode==0 (posix_fallocate) grows the file so its logical size is >= offset+len (never shrinking an already-larger file) via handle_path + Vfs::file_size/Vfs::truncate; mode==KEEP_SIZE reserves blocks for [0, offset+len) without changing the logical size via Vfs::fallocate. Both enforce RLIMIT_FSIZE (EFBIG, also on checked_add overflow) and the File-WRITE capability; MemFd fds grow via ipc::memfd::truncate (KEEP_SIZE is a no-op for in-memory backing). Every other surviving mode combination (PUNCH_HOLE, ZERO_RANGE, COLLAPSE_RANGE, INSERT_RANGE, UNSHARE_RANGE and valid combos) keeps the spec-acceptable EOPNOTSUPP fallback (sqlite/PostgreSQL treat it as "write zeros instead"), as does kernel context (caller_pid None — no fd table), so the batch-536 FMODE_WRITE + vfs_fallocate gate-order self-tests stay green. Self-test (Path Z Part 33, self_test_linux_fallocate): a hand-built raw-syscall ELF (build_linux_fallocate_grow_test_elf) open(O_RDWR)s /fallocate-test and calls fallocate(fd, 0, 0, 10) from ring 3 (sentinels 0xD1/0xD2); the harness stages the file at 4 bytes on the memfs root and, after the process exits 0, independently asserts Vfs::read_file reports a 10-byte file with the original 4 'A' bytes preserved and the grown tail zero-filled. Path Z Part 34 (real GNU make runs a recipe via /bin/sh — access()-stub fix + posix_spawn vfork clone support) (2026-06-16): unmodified prebuilt GNU make 4.3 (glibc, dynamically linked) now runs end-to-end in ring 3: ld.so loads make+libc, make parses a Makefile, and dispatches its recipe through /bin/sh, which fork/exec's /bin/emit with a `>` redirect — the first rung of the GCC/CMake/Make toolchain initiative. Two real kernel bugs were fixed. (1) THE access() STUB (root cause): sys_access/sys_faccessat/sys_faccessat2 unconditionally returned ENOENT (stale no-backing-FS skeleton), so make's `access("/bin/sh", X_OK)` — which it issues BEFORE spawning the recipe shell — always failed and make bailed with `"/bin/sh: No such file or directory"` / `Error 127` without ever spawning (confirmed by strace ground truth on real Linux: `access(shell, X_OK) = 0` precedes the clone3). The three syscalls now share a new access_path_common back-end that canonicalises the path against the caller's cwd and looks it up via Vfs::metadata/lmetadata (follow honours AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW). Under our capability-based, no-DAC security model F_OK/R_OK/X_OK succeed for any existing file or dir — reporting X_OK as grantable is *consistent* with execve, which itself ignores on-disk execute bits (design-decisions §27). Kernel context (caller_pid None) preserves the ENOENT no-file contract the fidelity self-tests assert. (2) posix_spawn's clone: glibc posix_spawn issues `clone3({flags=CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK|CLONE_CLEAR_SIGHAND, exit_signal=SIGCHLD, stack=..., stack_size=...})`. validate_clone3_args rejected CLONE_CLEAR_SIGHAND with EINVAL (now accepted — honoured by resetting the child's kernel-side signal state, though the imminent execve resets it anyway), and linux_clone_inner had no path for CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK (no CLONE_THREAD) with a caller-provided child stack. A new VFORK_SPAWN branch degenerates this to a copy-on-write fork (our processes are address-space isolated, so a shared-VM vfork is impossible) with the child resuming on the caller's child_stack per clone(2); fork.rs grew fork_process_vfork / fork_process_clone_inner(rsp_override) for this. Known degradation (known-issues): on exec FAILURE in the child the errno written to the Linux-shared stack is lost under CoW, so the parent observes a 127 child exit rather than the precise errno. Self-test (self_test_linux_real_glibc_make — since 2026-09-16 `self_test_linux_slateos_make`): stages ld/libc/make/sh/emit from the /mnt ext4 rootfs, writes a Makefile whose recipe is `@/bin/emit > /make-out.txt`, runs `make -f /Makefile all`, and asserts exit 0 with /make-out.txt == the 16-byte emit body. Path Z Part 35 (real prebuilt C compiler — TinyCC/tcc — compiles C to a native ELF that runs in ring 3; bare-static-binary ABI-detection fix) (2026-06-18): an unmodified prebuilt `tcc` (glibc, dynamically linked against libc+libm) now runs in ring 3, compiles a freestanding C source into an x86_64 ELF, and that freshly-built ELF then *also* runs in ring 3 and produces correct output — proving the OS can host a real toolchain, not merely run prebuilt binaries. Flow (self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc): stage ld/libc/libm/tcc from the /mnt ext4 rootfs, write a `-nostdlib` freestanding C program (own `_start`, raw write/exit syscalls, message built on the stack), run `tcc -nostdlib -static -o /cc-prog /cc-prog.c` (ld.so loads tcc+libc+libm, tcc codegens a 1300-byte ELF), then spawn `/cc-prog` directly with its fd 1 redirected to a capture file (the proven linux_fd_take + linux_fd_install_at mechanism) and assert it wrote the 16-byte `SLATE_TCC_CC_OK\n` payload, exit 0. One real kernel gap was fixed: a bare static binary tcc emits for the Linux ABI carries NO marker `elf::detect_linux_abi` recognises (OSABI=SYSV/0, no PT_INTERP, no PT_GNU_PROPERTY — only a PT_GNU_RELRO segment, which is deliberately not a signal), so it was misclassified as a Native-ABI process and its `write`/`exit` syscalls were routed through the wrong dispatch table (the `write(1,…)` produced 0 observable bytes — confirmed via the new exit-code/byte-count diagnostic). Fix: added `spawn::spawn_process_with_abi(elf, options, AbiMode::Linux)` — a thin `spawn_process` variant (zero call-site churn: both wrap a shared `spawn_process_inner` taking an `Option<AbiMode>` override) that lets a caller which *knows* the binary's ABI (because it just produced it with a known toolchain) state it explicitly instead of relying on a heuristic that cannot see the difference. The broader question of how the OS should auto-classify arbitrary *wild* bare static ELFs (Linux vs SlateOS-native) is escalated to the operator as open-questions.md Q9 (recommendation: default unmarked bare ELFs to Linux ABI and stamp native binaries with an explicit SlateOS OSABI/note). Path Z Part 36 (real prebuilt C compiler — tcc — now performs a HOSTED glibc-linked compile: links a C program against real glibc through crt startup + ld.so into a *dynamically-linked* ELF that runs in ring 3; zero-length-read POSIX fix) (2026-06-18): the hosted complement to Part 35's `-nostdlib -static` freestanding compile. An unmodified prebuilt `tcc` now runs `tcc -o /hosted-prog /hosted-prog.c` against the real glibc support set (crt1.o/crti.o/crtn.o + libc.so linker-script + libc_nonshared.a + libtcc1.a, all staged from the /mnt ext4 rootfs by scripts/create-ext4-rootfs.sh), producing a 4135-byte ELF with `PT_INTERP=/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`. Because the output carries PT_INTERP it is auto-classified Linux-ABI (no explicit override needed, unlike Part 35's bare static binary), so the run step is a plain `spawn_process`; ld.so then loads the freshly-built binary + libc, `main` calls libc `puts`, and the exit-time stdio flush writes the expected 20-byte `SLATE_TCC_HOSTED_OK
`, exit 0. One real kernel bug was fixed (root-caused via strace ground-truth on Linux): tcc's `full_read` reads exactly `count` bytes and then issues a *terminal* `read(fd, buf, 0)`, relying on POSIX's rule that a zero-length read returns 0; SlateOS's `sys_fs_read` instead rejected `buf_cap == 0` with EINVAL, so `full_read` propagated the negative result and `tcc_object_type` saw a short ELF-header read and rejected *every* relocatable object (crt1.o, crti.o, …) as "unrecognized file type" (the `.c` source read fine because it never issues a terminal zero-read). Fix: `sys_fs_read` now returns 0 for a zero-length read without validating/touching the buffer (matching Linux `read(fd, NULL, 0) == 0`), before the null-pointer check — proper for both the native and Linux ABIs. Self-test (self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_hosted): no-ops cleanly if the glibc support set is absent; otherwise parses tcc's output and asserts it is dynamically linked (interp present) before running it with fd 1 redirected via the linux_fd_take + linux_fd_install_at capture mechanism. Path Z Part 37 (hosted tcc compile exercising more glibc ABI — printf varargs + heap) (2026-06-19): strengthens Part 36 by compiling+running a freshly-tcc-built dynamic binary that does a malloc/free heap round-trip and a printf with variadic format conversions (`%s` consumes a pointer arg, `%d` formats an int) — the program builds a string on the heap (`malloc(8)` → 'SLATE'), prints `printf("%s-%d
", p, 1234)`, frees it, returns 0. Because fd 1 is redirected to a regular file (not a tty) glibc makes stdout fully buffered, so the printf output is emitted by the exit-time flush — the same path Part 36 validates for puts. tcc produced a 4455-byte dynamic ELF (PT_INTERP set), ld.so loaded it + libc, and the captured output was exactly the 11-byte `SLATE-1234
`, exit 0. No kernel changes needed (the Part 36 zero-length-read fix + the existing dynamic-load / glibc-init path already cover it). Refactor: the Part 36/37 harness was factored into a shared run_hosted_cc_case(label, src, expect_out) back-end (stages the glibc support set, compiles, asserts the output is dynamically linked, runs with fd-1 capture, asserts the bytes) so each rung is a thin ~3-line caller. Path Z Part 38 (separate compilation — tcc -c objects + multi-object link) (2026-06-19): strengthens Parts 36/37, which each compiled+linked a single source in one tcc invocation, by exercising tcc's object emission AND tcc-as-linker over multiple relocatable inputs. Flow (self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_separate): `tcc -c /sep-a.c -o /sep-a.o` (compile-only TU A, defines slate_add) then `tcc -c /sep-b.c -o /sep-b.o` (compile-only TU B, whose main calls slate_add across the TU boundary), each verified to be a real relocatable ELF object via a new assert_relocatable_elf helper (ELF magic + e_type==ET_REL(1) at offset 0x10 — proving `-c` produced an object, not an executable); then `tcc -o /sep-prog /sep-a.o /sep-b.o` links both relocatables + crt + glibc into one dynamic executable, resolving the cross-TU slate_add reference at link time (asserted PT_INTERP-bearing dynamic ELF). tcc emitted a 1179-byte and a 1494-byte ET_REL object and a 4295-byte dynamic ELF; ld.so ran it with fd 1 redirected to a capture file and the exit-time stdio flush wrote exactly the 13-byte `SLATE-SEP-42` line, exit 0. No kernel changes needed (the Part 36 zero-length-read fix + the existing dynamic-load/glibc-init path already cover it). Refactor: the Part 36/37 single-file harness (formerly run_hosted_cc_case inline) was further factored into four shared helpers — stage_hosted_cc_support, spawn_reap_tcc, assert_dynamic_elf, run_dynamic_capture — reused by all three rungs; Part 38 composes them across its three tcc invocations plus assert_relocatable_elf. Path Z Part 39 (the §4.4 toolchain capstone — real GNU make drives tcc to build a multi-file C program) (2026-06-19): composes Part 34 (real make in ring 3) with Part 38 (tcc separate compilation) into the realistic "build a C project with make + a compiler" flow. Flow (self_test_linux_real_glibc_make_cc — since 2026-09-16 `self_test_linux_slateos_make_cc`): stage the hosted-cc support set plus /bin/make and /bin/sh from the /mnt rootfs, write two TUs (/cap-a.c defines slate_add, /cap-b.c's main calls it across the boundary) and a 3-target Makefile (/cap-prog: /cap-a.o /cap-b.o; each .o built by `tcc -c`; the program linked by `tcc -o`), then run `make -f /cap.mk all`. make parsed the prerequisite graph and fork/exec'd /bin/tcc three times — compiling the two TUs to relocatable objects and linking them + crt + glibc into a 4295-byte dynamic ELF — which then ran in ring 3 with fd 1 redirected to a capture file and the exit-time stdio flush wrote exactly the 13-byte `SLATE-SEP-42` line, exit 0. This is make *as the build driver* spawning the compiler across a real dependency graph (make + tcc×3 is the heaviest multi-process glibc workload in the suite, budget 33,554,432 yields). No kernel changes needed (Part 34's posix_spawn/access fixes + the Part 36 zero-length-read fix already cover it). With this rung the hosted-toolchain line is functionally complete; the next step (compiling sources that `#include <stdio.h>`) is BLOCKED on staging the glibc header tree into the rootfs, which neither the image nor the build host currently carries (documented in todo.txt). Path Z Part 40 (project-local `#include "..."` across multiple TUs) (2026-06-19): self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_project_header writes a shared include-guarded header (a macro SLATE_BASE + a cross-TU prototype) and two TUs that each `#include "caphdr-hdr.h"`, then `tcc -o prog a.c b.c` resolves the quote-include, expands the macro, honors the prototype across the TU boundary, and the linked dynamic ELF prints SLATE-HDR-42 in ring 3 — filling the header-include gap left by Parts 36-39 (which used bare `extern`s) for the project-relative quote form (the `<system_header.h>` glibc-tree form stays blocked per TD22). Path Z Part 41 (C-runtime constructor/destructor lifecycle) (2026-07-15): self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_ctor_dtor is the first rung to exercise `.init_array`/`.fini_array` — a program with `__attribute__((constructor))` and `__attribute__((destructor))` (tcc emits them into those sections) prints three raw `write(2)` markers; glibc's csu init (`__libc_csu_init`, called by `__libc_start_main` before `main`) walks `.init_array` and the dynamic linker's `_dl_fini` walks `.fini_array` at exit, so the captured file is exactly `CTOR\nMAIN\nDTOR\n` (15 bytes, exit 0) — proving the full ctor→main→dtor lifecycle for a real dynamically-linked glibc program in ring 3. Unbuffered write(2) (not stdio) makes the byte order the exact temporal order, immune to exit-time-flush-vs-.fini_array ordering ambiguity. No kernel changes needed (reuses the Part 36 run_hosted_cc_case harness). Path Z Part 42 (ELF thread-local storage in a compiled binary) (2026-07-15): self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_tls is the first rung to exercise the TLS ABI from *tcc output* (the pre-existing pthread self-test runs a pre-built /bin/pthread, not compiled-on-target code). tcc emits a `.tdata`/PT_TLS segment + local-exec TLS relocations for an initialised `__thread int` (42); glibc's `__libc_setup_tls` copies the PT_TLS init image (found via AT_PHDR/AT_PHNUM) into the main thread's TLS block, and `%fs`-relative access reads it — the program prints `slate_tls % 10` (=2), reassigns it to 7, and prints again (=7) so the captured file is exactly `27\n` (3 bytes, exit 0), proving the init image was copied AND the block is writable. Path Z Part 43 (POSIX signal delivery in a compiled binary) (2026-07-15): self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_signal is the first rung to drive the kernel's Linux signal machinery (`rt_sigaction`, asynchronous signal-frame setup, `rt_sigreturn`) from *tcc output* — the pre-existing signal self-tests (self_test_linux_real_glibc_signal / _sigqueue / _fault) run pre-built ELFs, so no prior rung proved the full "tcc emits a `.text` handler → glibc's `signal()` installs it via `rt_sigaction` (with glibc's SA_RESTORER trampoline) → `raise()` issues `tgkill` → the kernel posts the signal and, on the syscall-return path, builds the Linux signal frame the handler `ret`s into to reach `rt_sigreturn`" round-trip for a binary compiled on-target. Unbuffered write(2) makes the byte order the exact temporal order. No kernel changes needed (reuses the Part 36 run_hosted_cc_case harness); it is the signal-delivery sibling of Part 41 (ctor/dtor) and Part 42 (TLS). Path Z Part 44 (non-local control flow — setjmp/longjmp) (2026-07-15): self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_setjmp is the first rung to exercise C's non-local jump (the substrate for error-recovery / exception-like unwinding). Proves tcc emits the correct `_setjmp`/`_longjmp` call sequence and glibc's callee-saved-register + `%rsp`/`%rip` save/restore works in ring 3. No kernel changes needed. Path Z Part 45 (user-defined variadic function — SysV varargs ABI codegen) (2026-07-15): self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_vararg is the first rung to exercise tcc's *own* lowering of the x86_64 variadic ABI (register save area, `%al` vector-register count on the call side, `va_start`/`va_arg`/`va_end` bookkeeping) for a *user-authored* variadic function — a path printf never covers (its `va_arg` walk lives inside glibc). Pure userspace/codegen (no kernel path); value is proving tcc's variadic ABI lowering produces a correct binary here. No kernel changes needed. Path Z Part 46 (floating-point / SSE codegen + SysV FP ABI) (2026-07-15): self_test_linux_real_glibc_cc_float is the first rung to use floating point — Parts 34-45 never touched an XMM register, so tcc's `double` codegen (`mulsd`/`addsd`), the SysV FP calling convention (args/return in `%xmm0`/`%xmm1`), and the truncating `double`→`int` cast (`cvttsd2si`) were untested from compiled code. Pure userspace/codegen; value is proving tcc's FP codegen + SysV FP ABI produce a correct ring-3 binary (and XMM state is sane across the glibc call path). With this rung the compiled-language-feature coverage (control flow, ctor/dtor, TLS, signals, setjmp/longjmp, varargs, floating point) is comprehensive; the remaining gaps are compiled-pthread (deferred while B-PTHREAD-TEARDOWN-PF is open) and the `<system_header.h>` glibc-tree include form (blocked per TD22). No kernel changes needed. REMAINING (TD22 Phase 2) is won't-fix per design-decisions §22; ongoing per-syscall behavioural fidelity tuning.

/proc/<pid>/status rewritten to Linux key:value format, /proc/self symlink, /proc/<pid>/maps from the VMA list (committed + lazy mmap both register a VMA), and /proc/<pid>/mountinfo in Linux 11-field show_mountinfo format for findmnt/glibc/systemd (2026-06-10);
