every other procfs path stays read-only), schedstat (real per-task TSC cpu_ns / run-queue wait / dispatch count), and loginuid/sessionid (audit "unset" = u32::MAX) (2026-06-10); /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/ thread dirs implemented (nested-dir routing in classify_path + per-thread comm/schedstat/stat/status, thread fields keyed by tid and process-wide fields by owning pid) (2026-06-11); /proc/<pid>/status extended with genuinely-backed NoNewPrivs, Seccomp, Cpus_allowed/Cpus_allowed_list (per-thread affinity) and Mems_allowed/Mems_allowed_list (all online NUMA nodes), Name/comm truncated to 15 bytes, with stat<->status State-char consistency self-tested (2026-06-11); system-wide /proc/stat converted from a custom native format to the real Linux fs/proc/stat.c layout (cpu/cpuN jiffy lines from real per-CPU TSC accounting in cputime, intr/ctxt/btime/processes/procs_running/procs_blocked/softirq), with a new monotonic fork counter (pcb::processes_created) and zeros for genuinely-untracked columns — never fabricated (2026-06-11); /proc/uptime converted to the Linux fs/proc/uptime.c two-field "<uptime> <idle>" centisecond format, idle summed across all CPUs from cputime's real per-CPU TSC idle accounting (2026-06-11); /proc/loadavg converted from instantaneous-runnable-in-all-three-slots to real Linux 1/5/15-minute EWMAs — scheduler's update_load_average now maintains three fixed-point averages with Linux's exact FSHIFT/EXP_1/EXP_5/EXP_15 constants, sampled every 5s (LOAD_FREQ) from O(1) per-CPU queue lengths, formatted <int>.<frac> like Linux LOAD_INT/LOAD_FRAC (2026-06-11); /proc/buddyinfo cleaned to the pure Linux mm/vmstat.c frag_show layout (real per-order buddy free-block counts; dropped the non-Linux trailing "# Order sizes"/"# Total free frames" comment lines that broke strict parsers) (2026-06-11); /proc/<pid>/io implemented with honest per-process counters — four new PCB u64 counters (rchar/wchar/syscr/syscw) incremented at the Linux-ABI read/write syscall boundary (dispatch_linux → account_io_syscall classifying the read/write/pread/pwrite/readv/writev/preadv/pwritev(+2) family exactly as Linux folds into task io accounting), served via gen_pid_io in the Linux 7-line key:value layout with the three storage-layer fields (read_bytes/write_bytes/cancelled_write_bytes) reported as 0 (genuinely untracked, never fabricated); increment logic self-tested in kernel context (pcb::test_io_accounting) plus formatter+path self-test (2026-06-11); native-ABI io accounting now also wired — syscall::dispatch::dispatch folds completed native read/write syscalls (FS_READ/FS_READ_FILE, PIPE_READ/_TRY_READ/_READ_TIMEOUT, CONSOLE_READ_CHAR/_TRY_READ_CHAR; FS_WRITE, PIPE_WRITE/_TRY_WRITE/_WRITE_TIMEOUT, CONSOLE_WRITE) into the same account_io_{read,write} via a pure unit-tested io_dir_for_syscall classifier, reusing the task_id already resolved for the syscall filter (FS_WRITE_FILE deliberately excluded — returns 0 not a byte count), so native processes get real io counters instead of all-zero; native and Linux-ABI dispatch are separate entry paths so no double-counting (2026-06-11); /proc/<pid>/fd/ directory + per-fd magic symlinks added — backed by the real per-process Linux KernelFdTable (new list_open enumerator + pcb::linux_fd_list accessor), each fd/<n> resolving to its backing object's target (File→VFS path via fs::handle::handle_path, Pipe→pipe:[id], Console→/dev/console, eventfd/pidfd/memfd→anon_inode:[type]); the directory is honestly empty for native processes whose fd table lives in userspace and is not kernel-visible (2026-06-11); /proc/<pid>/fdinfo/<n> added alongside fd/ — regular files rendering Linux's pos:/flags: lines (pos = the open-file description's real f_pos via fs::handle::current_offset for File fds, 0 for non-seekable objects as on Linux; flags reproduces fs/proc/fd.c by folding the descriptor's FD_CLOEXEC into O_CLOEXEC), deliberately omitting mnt_id/ino rather than fabricating them since key-based readers like lsof/CRIU look up pos:/flags: by name; same honestly-empty-for-native behaviour (2026-06-12); /proc/<pid>/auxv now served by gen_pid_auxv from the per-process saved auxv that the Linux SysV initial-stack builder persists into pcb::linux_saved_auxv at spawn/exec — the raw Elf64_auxv_t byte stream for Linux-ABI pids, an honestly-empty file for native pids (which have no auxv by design), added to PID_FILES so it lists and resolves (2026-06-12). **/proc/sys sysctl tree added (2026-06-13)** — the first nested-directory subtree besides per-PID `task/`/`fd/`. New `SYS_FILES`/`SYS_DIRS` flat tables + two `ProcPath` variants (`SysDir`/`SysFile`) routed in `classify_path` (intercepted before the numeric-PID parse since "sys" isn't a number); `sys_immediate_child`/`sys_basename`/`sys_children` enumerate interior dirs from the flat tables. Files served by `gen_sys`, all real-backed (never fabricated): `kernel/{ostype,osrelease,version,hostname,domainname}` are the exact `uname(2)` surface (byte-consistent with `sys_uname` — "Linux"/"6.6.0-slateos"/"#1 SMP"/nameservice hostname+domain), `kernel/pid_max`=`pidns::MAX_PIDS_PER_NS`, `fs/nr_open`=`linux_fd::MAX_FDS`, and `kernel/random/{uuid,boot_id}` generated from the kernel CSPRNG per Linux semantics (uuid fresh per read; boot_id stable per boot via a cached `spin::Once`, RFC 4122 v4 with forced version/variant bits). `/proc` root readdir now lists the `sys` directory; tree is read-only (only `oom_score_adj` honours writes). 10-case classify test + listing/value/kind/UUID self-tests ("[procfs]   /proc/sys: ... OK"). This is what systemd/D-Bus/glibc/WINE read for kernel identity, machine session id, and fd/pid ceilings. Extended with `kernel/random/{poolsize,entropy_avail}` (2026-06-13): poolsize is the fixed 256-bit ceiling matching our ChaCha20 CSPRNG seed width (= Linux POOL_BITS since ~5.18), entropy_avail reports 256 once `rng::is_initialized()` (0 before init) so userspace can tell the random source is ready; both parsed + bounds-checked (0|256, ≤poolsize) in the self-test. **/proc/cpuinfo converted to the real Linux per-processor format (2026-06-13)** — `gen_cpuinfo` previously emitted a custom layout (a `processors:`/`flags:`/`tsc_freq:` header block followed by per-CPU blocks keyed on `acpi_id`/`apic_id`/`enabled`/`online_cap`), which broke every standard consumer: `grep -c ^processor`/nproc/locale counted the `processors:` header line as an extra CPU (off-by-one overcount), and lscpu/hwinfo (which split blocks on blank lines) parsed the header block as a phantom CPU#0 with empty vendor/model, while glibc/toolchains found none of the keys they look for. Rewritten to one Linux-style block per online logical CPU, each beginning `processor\t: N` and carrying vendor_id/cpu family/model/model name/stepping/cpu MHz/cache size/physical id/siblings/core id/cpu cores/apicid/initial apicid/fpu/flags/bogomips/clflush size/cache_alignment — sourced from `cpu::vendor_string`/`brand_string`/`cpu_family_model_stepping`/`features`/`cache_topology` + `bench::tsc_freq` (a shared `push_cpu_flags` emits the Linux baseline + CPUID-detected flag tokens per block). Dropping the header block makes block-counting parsers count exactly the online-CPU count, fixing the off-by-one in native lscpu/nproc/locale/hwinfo and making Linux-binary cpuinfo parsing work. New procfs self-test asserts block count == `acpi::processor_count()`, first line `processor\t: 0`, per-block keys (vendor_id/cpu family/model name/flags/cpu cores) each appear once per CPU, and no legacy header keys remain ("[procfs]   cpuinfo: N Linux-format processor block(s) OK").
- [-] `[D]` ALSA/PulseAudio compatibility shim — kernel-level ALSA (`/dev/snd/*`) device emulation so unmodified Linux audio clients (ALSA-lib, and PA/PipeWire/JACK/SDL/WINE which all layer on ALSA) drive the SlateOS software mixer. **PCM side (`/dev/snd/pcmC0D0p`|`c`):** pure ABI layer kernel/src/audio_alsa.rs (ioctl request-number encoding, byte-exact `#[repr(C)]` mirrors of every `asound.h` payload struct, format/rate/access constants, exhaustive boot self-test); per-open substream instance object kernel/src/ipc/alsa_pcm.rs (refcounted create/dup/close, OPEN→SETUP→PREPARED→RUNNING→… state machine reserving an audio_mixer slot, frame write path to the mixer ring, capture-silence read path, position tracking); HandleKind::AlsaPcm fd family wired through linux.rs/linux_fd/cap/fork/procfs/cleanup + every exhaustive match site; ioctl dispatch covering PVERSION/INFO/HW_REFINE/HW_PARAMS/SW_PARAMS/HW_FREE/PREPARE/START/DROP/DRAIN/RESET/PAUSE/WRITEI_FRAMES/READI_FRAMES/SYNC_PTR/STATUS/STATUS_EXT (+HWSYNC/RESUME/XRUN/UNLINK/TTSTAMP no-ops); SYNC_PTR (the timestamp-ABI-independent per-period pointer exchange ALSA-lib's kernel plugin relies on) reports appl_ptr/hw_ptr from the mixer's buffered-frame count; STATUS/STATUS_EXT (2026-07-15) return a byte-exact `snd_pcm_status` (time64 ABI, `size_of==152`, `STATUS=0x8098_4120`/`STATUS_EXT=0xC098_4124` — see design-decisions.md §67) filling state/appl_ptr/hw_ptr/**delay** (queued frames, what `snd_pcm_delay(3)` needs for A/V sync)/**avail** (playback: free buffer space from the HW_PARAMS-negotiated BUFFER_SIZE; capture: full buffer) from the same snapshot as SYNC_PTR, plus monotonic reference timestamps and the trigger_tstamp stamped at START. **Control side (`/dev/snd/controlC0`):** pure ABI layer kernel/src/audio_alsa_ctl.rs ('U'-magic ioctls, snd_ctl_card_info/elem_id/elem_list/elem_info/elem_value byte-exact structs, element type/iface/access constants, card-element model + resolve_numid/elem_id_for/fill_elem_info helpers, exhaustive self-test); stateless HandleKind::AlsaControl fd (no per-open resource — a pure window onto the global mixer, mirroring Console/PidFd — wired through every match site); ioctl dispatch covering PVERSION, CARD_INFO (SlateOS card identity), and ELEM_LIST/ELEM_INFO/ELEM_READ/ELEM_WRITE mapping the two master controls (Master Playback Volume INTEGER 0..100, Master Playback Switch BOOLEAN) to audio_mixer master_volume/mute. This makes the card *visible* to `snd_ctl_open()` (alsamixer/amixer/PulseAudio's ALSA backend) and lets it read/set master volume + mute. **REMAINING:** ~~real hardware-backend audio output~~ **done 2026-10-02 on lane-a-wip (§1520):** the `audio_out` pump feeds Intel HD Audio, virtio-sound or AC'97 from the mixer, and native programs reach both nodes through the device door (`SYS_DEVICE_*`); capture and `XRUN` remain (known-issues `A-SOUND-CAPTURE-HAS-NO-SOURCE`, `A-PCM-UNDERRUN-IS-SILENT`); and a userspace PulseAudio-protocol daemon is an *alternative* shape (not needed — providing ALSA covers PA/PipeWire/JACK/SDL/WINE with one interface, see todo.txt design note).

### 5.2 Additional filesystems
- [-] `[A]` Port Btrfs (CoW, snapshots, checksums) — **read side done
  (2026-08-16), write side deliberately not started.** `kernel/src/fs/btrfs/`:
  the mount bootstrap that makes Btrfs awkward (superblock at a fixed physical
  64 KiB → `sys_chunk_array` → chunk tree → root tree → `FS_TREE_OBJECTID`'s
  root item → the FS tree), CRC32C metadata checksums, the logical→physical
  chunk map for every non-striped profile (single/DUP/RAID1/RAID1C3/RAID1C4;
  RAID0/10/5/6 refused at parse time), generic B-tree descent with `search` /
  `next` / `prev` over both leaves and internal nodes, and the leaf items a
  reader needs (`INODE_ITEM`, `INODE_REF`, `DIR_ITEM`/`DIR_INDEX` incl. hash
  collisions packed into one item, `EXTENT_DATA` inline/regular/prealloc,
  `ROOT_ITEM`). Four independent per-block validations — checksum, `bytenr`,
  `generation`, and `nritems`-fits-the-block — because each catches something
  the others cannot, the generation check specifically being the CoW hazard
  that a stale node still checksums correctly. Holes (NO_HOLES) and PREALLOC
  read as zeroes; compressed/encrypted extents are `NotSupported`, never
  returned raw. Full `FileSystem` impl (readdir / read_file / read_at / stat /
  lstat / metadata / lmetadata / readlink / statvfs / debug_stats) reporting
  `read_only: true` and `0o555`-masked modes. Reads through the shared
  `fs::blocksrc::SectorSource`, so the self-test drives the whole driver over a
  synthetic in-RAM volume on **every** boot with no device attached (7 test
  groups; logical and physical addresses are deliberately a constant 0x080000
  apart so a broken chunk map cannot accidentally produce correct reads).
  Mountable as `-t btrfs` from kshell, `SYS_FS_MOUNT`, and by `auto` probe.
  Snapshots are readable as ordinary subvolume trees; *creating* them is write
  support. See `design-decisions.md` §215.
- [-] `[A]` Port F2FS (SSD optimization) — **read side done (2026-08-16), write
  side deliberately not started.** `kernel/src/fs/f2fs/`: the superblock at a
  fixed byte 1024 with its backup at 5120 and a CRC that is Linux's bare
  `crc32_le` seeded with the magic (neither initial nor final inversion), the
  two-pack checkpoint with recovery by *version*, the NAT (node address table)
  indirection that turns a node id into a block, and the multi-level block
  path. Three indirections make F2FS reads hard, and each is a place a driver
  can silently return the wrong bytes rather than fail: (1) which of the two
  checkpoint packs is current — decided by version, but a pack only counts as
  valid if the version in its **first and last** block agree, which is what
  catches a half-written pack that still checksums; (2) which of the two NAT
  copies the checkpoint's NAT bitmap selects, via the interleaved address
  `nat_blkaddr + (off << 1) - (off & (blocks_per_seg-1))`; (3) whether the
  checkpoint's own NAT journal overrides both — it does, unconditionally, and
  it lives in a different place and format depending on whether the pack is
  compacted (`CP_COMPACT_SUM_FLAG`) or normal. Also: node footers (the footer
  nid is the only guard on the NAT indirection, so it is checked, and
  `read_inode` additionally requires footer `ino == nid`), inline data and
  inline dentries with their derived geometry, inline xattrs and
  `i_extra_isize` shifting `addrs_per_inode`, the TEA-with-MD4-IV name hash and
  the multi-level hashed directory bucket layout, and holes (`NULL_ADDR`) and
  prealloc (`NEW_ADDR`) both reading as zeroes. `FEATURE_BLKZONED` is refused
  at mount rather than mis-read. Full `FileSystem` impl (readdir / read_file /
  read_at / stat / lstat / metadata / lmetadata / readlink / statvfs /
  debug_stats) reporting `read_only: true` and `0o555`-masked modes. Reads
  through the shared `fs::blocksrc` sources, so the self-test drives the whole
  driver over a synthetic in-RAM volume on **every** boot with no device
  attached (8 test groups). Each of the three indirections above carries a
  deliberate **decoy** in that volume — NAT copy 0 is all `NULL_ADDR`,
  `hello.txt`'s NAT-area entry points at a valid-but-stale inode that only the
  journal supersedes, and the two packs disagree in both version and summary
  layout — so a driver that gets one wrong fails a named check instead of
  returning plausible bytes from the wrong block. Mountable as `-t f2fs` from
  kshell, `SYS_FS_MOUNT`, and by `auto` probe. See `design-decisions.md` §216.
- [-] `[A]` NTFS read/write support — **read side done (2026-08-16), write side
  deliberately not started.** `kernel/src/fs/ntfs/`: boot sector (incl. the
  signed power-of-two `clusters_per_mft_record`/`clusters_per_index_buffer`
  encodings), update-sequence fixups for `FILE` and `INDX`, MFT records,
  resident/non-resident attributes, variable-width sign-extended runlists with
  sparse runs, `$ATTRIBUTE_LIST` extension-record merging, `$STANDARD_INFORMATION`,
  `$FILE_NAME` with namespace handling (8.3 DOS aliases hidden), the `$I30`
  directory B+ tree across both `$INDEX_ROOT` and `$INDEX_ALLOCATION`,
  `$Volume` label/version, and the full `FileSystem` impl (readdir / read_file /
  read_at / stat / lstat / metadata / statvfs / debug_stats) reporting
  `read_only: true` and `0o444`/`0o555`. Compressed and encrypted `$DATA` are
  `NotSupported`, never returned raw. Reads through a `SectorSource` trait so
  the self-test drives the whole parser over a synthetic in-RAM volume on
  **every** boot with no device attached (8 test groups). Write support stays
  out until `$LogFile` journalling exists — see `design-decisions.md` §210.

    (`oci::commit_image` → `container::commit_image`). Distinct from the native
    `container commit`, which clones a container; `docker commit` stages a
    standalone layout in a temp dir then imports it into the store under the
    given `name:tag`.
    Real in-container `container exec` (spawns a genuine process in the
    container's namespaces + cgroup and, foreground, blocks on its exit via
    `wait_process`) and image `HEALTHCHECK` (parsed from OCI config, driven by
    a non-blocking hrtimer→workqueue supervisor, surfaced in `inspect`/`ps`)
    both shipped. Per operator decision Q17 (§58, option B): the netns-debug
    `container exec` facade is kept AND real rootfs-binary exec is added under a
    distinct verb (`container run-in` / `container exec --rootfs`); the `docker
    exec` delegate routes to the real path. Dockerfile `RUN` now executes via
    the real in-container exec pipeline (materialize lower rootfs → overlay
    create+mount → ephemeral container → `exec_path_env` → `wait_process` →
    capture the overlay upper as the new layer; failures map to
    `RunLaunch`/`RunFailed`), and Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` is parsed and
    serialized into the image config (`ImageSpec.healthcheck`, Go-duration flags,
    NONE/CMD/CMD-SHELL forms, FROM inheritance). Runtime `network
    connect/disconnect` shipped (Q19/§60, option B): the container network model
    is generalised to N-interface multi-network membership — a `Container` keeps
    its create-time primary veth plus a `memberships[]` list of named-network
    attachments (each with its own veth pair, IP, and connected route), exposed
    via `container network connect/disconnect <net> <ctr>` (+ `docker network
    connect/disconnect` delegate), surfaced in `container info`/`inspect`
    (`networks[]`), and covered by the `Multi-network membership (attach/detach)`
    boot self-test. Disconnecting the primary network is refused (its veth is
    lifecycle-owned). Honest limitation: the netns L3 config still tracks only the
    primary interface; additional networks provide L2 bridge reachability + IPAM
    lease + embedded DNS + a connected route.
  - [ ] `[A]` The Linux namespace calls, over the namespaces above: `unshare(2)`
    (`CLONE_NEWNS`, `NEWUTS`, `NEWIPC`, `NEWNET`, `NEWPID`, `NEWUSER`,
    `NEWCGROUP`, `NEWTIME`), `setns(2)`, `/proc/<pid>/ns/*` opening to namespace
    handles, `/proc/self/{uid_map,gid_map,setgroups}` for `--map-root-user`, and
    `mount(NULL, "/", NULL, MS_REC | MS_PRIVATE)` in a new mount namespace.
    Waiting on it: util-linux's `unshare` and `nsenter`, which refuse until then
    (`requests/b-ad-unshare-and-nsenter-wait-on-unshare-and-setns.md`), lane D's
    libc `unshare()`/`setns()`, and any later `runc`, `podman` or `bubblewrap`,
    which call the same set.

## Notes

- **Large-initiative ordering (operator-fixed 2026-07-18 — do NOT re-ask).** Now
  that the self-hosting C toolchain + POSIX layer are comprehensive, the remaining
  giant initiatives are executed in this fixed order (Q25 → design-decisions.md §69):
  1. **Oils (OSH) + coreutils** — the interactive-shell userland. Oils is a
     bash-*superset* shell (roadmap-detailed.md §2.7), **not** bash itself.
  2. **fastpy build-system integration** — unlocks the Python-via-fastpy userspace lane.
  3. **Mesa / GPU userspace (3D)** — gated by Q18 until a virgl test environment exists.
  4. **Chromium** — browser + system-web-app / Electron framework.
  5. **WINE** — Windows app compatibility.
  6. **Additional filesystems** — Btrfs / F2FS / NTFS.
  Pick the next one whenever the current initiative lands; the operator has already
  set the order, so there's no need to ask which comes next.
- **Don't write custom filesystems early.** Port ext4. Data loss bugs are unforgivable.
- **Don't write a custom browser.** Port Chromium. It's huge but unlocks three things at once.
- **GPU drivers are the hardest part.** Start with AMD (open source). Intel second. NVIDIA last (via Linux compat layer).
- **Benchmark everything.** Write benchmarks before optimizing. AI is good at optimization with a concrete target.
- **One scheduler is enough initially.** Define the trait interface, implement priority round-robin, add alternatives only if users need them.
- **Security model from day one.** Capabilities, IOMMU, CFI — bake these in early. Retrofitting security is much harder.
